Ancient Name (also: Ancient Names, tocaitl, Ancient Name stone, Ancient Name stones, Name bearer, Ancient Name bearer): An Ancient Name (tocaitl) is a title held by certain people of Natlan's six tribes, along with a small obsidian stone that represents it. Each Name stands for a quality such as blessing, devotion or resilience, and carries the remembered deeds of everyone who bore it before. The tribe's guardian spirit, its Wayob, picks who receives one. Before the war ended, bearers were expected to enter the Pilgrimage and to fight the Abyss in the Night Warden Wars.

The Name is both an honour and a way of keeping a tribe's history alive: each bearer's deeds become part of what the Name means for the next. Most Names are not tied to a single tribe. Natlan's people treat receiving one as a special honour, and bearers are the only people whom the Ode of Resurrection was originally meant to revive.

The Ancient Names carried by the six Heroes of Natlan are special: they are linked to a hero of the past, and a modern hero who truly connects with theirs gains that earlier hero's memories and knowledge. The Traveler received a Name of their own in Incandescent Ode of Resurrection (5.3), the first ever given to an outsider.

Most Ancient Names do not give powers. Pacal says the bearer must earn the Name's meaning by their own deeds. The Names are made in the syllabic form of the Ancient Teyvat Script, and the wiki traces the known words to Swahili; this is an out-of-universe note.

Receipt: Each tribe's Wayob is mainly responsible for granting Ancient Names to worthy tribe members. Xilonen says the recipient must have done something in their life that embodies the spirit of the Name, though the recipient may not understand why they were chosen. A Name is not usually limited to one tribe, apart from those of the Heroes of Natlan and Names bound to a particular tribe's own tradition.

The Pyro Archon can instead commission a new Name for someone they judge worthy, though strict conditions apply. A skilled smith trained as a Name Engraver does the work, and forging costs the engraver part of their lifespan. Xilonen says the forging technique is not hard but gathering the facts of the recipient's life must be careful and exact: any falsehood in it would make the Name defective and could cause cognitive problems for its bearer.

A Name can also be forged to record a deserving person's life after they have died, and the Wayob then give it to the first worthy recipient. It is unclear whether the Archon commissions these or how common they are. Normally only Natlanese memories are recorded by the Night Kingdom, so historically only people of Natlan received Names. For the Traveler, Mavuika promised one in recognition of rescuing Kachina and helping against the Abyss, and the Lord of the Night's Pilgrim's Chronicle solved the problem of recording their deeds (see the Traveler's Name below).

Stones: Each bearer receives an obsidian stone shaped like a feather. Glowing characters in the Ancient Teyvat Script appear on both faces and spell the Name in syllables. Bearers usually carry the stone, but this is not required: when Mualani led the rescue of Kachina from the Night Kingdom she chose to leave hers behind. Stones are made by commissioned Name Engravers such as Xilonen, and formerly her mentor Tlazolli. Forging also engraves the deeds of the Name's first bearer into the stone, though these marks are not visible on the finished object. The story implies that a Name must be stored in such a stone and cannot exist alone.

The wiki suggests the feather shape may echo the bird-like design of Wayob Manifestations. This is a guess, not stated in canon. Xilonen says that using an Ancient Name to commit a crime was unheard of, until Tlazolli was caught trying to overwrite Nepecha's memories with those of his late daughter Nechca, a case the Children of Echoes had not yet resolved when it was recorded.

Duties: While the Night Warden Wars lasted, bearers had to take part in the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, and those who won a place were normally sent to fight the Abyss.

Team leaders were usually bearers, and a team with several bearers was uncommon because it could look like cowardice. The Archon could release a winner, as happened to Vichama after an injury. Illness or old injuries could bar a bearer from the Pilgrimage, as with Atea and Chanca. If at least one member of a team returned victorious, the Ode of Resurrection could revive the fallen. If a whole team fell, none came back, their deeds were forgotten and their Names lost, which is why the saying goes that victors burn bright while the defeated turn to ash.

Bearers could keep competing as long as they felt able. The most famous holder of Uthabiti had fought in twenty-seven Night Warden Wars and was past sixty when Pacal described him, which Pacal called exceptional. A Name can also be lost by being unclaimed: Mavuika says the exile Tenoch lost his while still alive. New Names forged over time have replaced those lost in the Wars.

Known names: The Names with known meanings, each with its current bearer in the story: Baraka (blessing, Xilonen), Bidii (devotion, Ororon), Kiongozi (leader, Mavuika), Malipo (the Turnfire, Kinich), Mwongozo (guidance, bearer unknown), Tumaini (hope, the Traveler), Ukumbuko (memory, Citlali), Umoja (unity, Mualani), Undugu (kinship, Tlazolli), Uthabiti (resilience, Kachina), Uwezo (power, Iansan) and Vuka (transcension, Chasca). A thirteenth Name meaning "seek" was last held by Vichama; he died in the Archon Quest and no successor has been named.

Earlier bearers listed by the wiki: Baraka, Sundjatta, Sakkuk and Ixquieh. Bidii, Sanhaj Kompore. Kiongozi, Xbalanque. Malipo, Burkina and Yupanqui. Ukumbuko, Huitzilin and the master of Maghan. Umoja, Tupac and Uenuku. Uwezo, Wanjiru and Ahpub. Vuka, Menilek and Lianca. Known bearers whose Names are not given include Cauich, Chanca, Kibangu and Kaiulani (current), and Atea, Mallko, Pisac and Tenoch (former). These attributions come from a wiki table that cites individual quests and weapon texts; treat Ukumbuko's and Undugu's as medium confidence.

Six heroes: Six Names belong to the Heroes of Natlan: Baraka, Bidii, Malipo, Umoja, Uwezo and Vuka. Their bearers 500 years ago were Sundjatta, Sanhaj Kompore, Burkina, Tupac, Wanjiru and Menilek. Today they are held by Xilonen, Ororon, Kinich, Mualani, Iansan and Chasca. Each modern hero was recognised through the Name before the Wayob formally acknowledged them, as part of Mavuika's plan to end the war.

Mavuika told the Traveler that after the Cataclysm the tribes and their Wayob were weakened, and a Wayob picking a bearer showed the tribe was strong again. By the time the Traveler arrived, Kinich, Iansan and Xilonen were ready; Mualani made a fourth, and the story later brought in Ororon and, after her sister Chuychu died in the invasion, Chasca. The wiki says Name Engravers adjusted these six Names so that connecting with one brings back the memories of its earlier holders.

Travelers name: Mavuika arranged for Xilonen to forge a Name for the Traveler. Xilonen at first called it impossible because the Night Kingdom does not record an outsider's deeds. With help from Citlali and the Lord of the Night, who made a parchment called the Pilgrim's Chronicle to record the Traveler's past and future deeds in Natlan, she forged Tumaini, "hope". The Traveler's soul proved so strong that testing it drew in many stray souls, including Vichama.

When the Traveler embodied Natlan's hope in the final battle, a projection of the Name appeared and the Lord of the Night acknowledged it with a mantra, unlocking their Nightsoul's Blessing. The mantra speaks of someone setting themselves aflame in darkness so that the universe could know light.

Mantras: Every Name has a mantra, usually revealed in a dream to a tribe's chief by a Wayob. Those known outside the Heroes of Natlan are paraphrased here. Tumaini is about the first person to burn in the dark so that light could exist. Ukumbuko, probably Citlali's, speaks of a bird-like soul that travels through forest, sea, fire and ore, whose paintings become gifts for the dead. Undugu, probably Tlazolli's, says the old gives rise to the new as flowers protect roots, until all return to the soil. Uthabiti tells of one who stands like a mountain, meets the sun's gaze and burns away what is petty. The wiki marks Ukumbuko's and Undugu's as likely rather than confirmed.

Status as of 7 1: After the final battle in 5.3 the Night Warden Wars are over. The Pilgrimage is now purely a competition, and bearers no longer have to take part in it. Ancient Names still exist and are still carried and honoured.

The Traveler holds Tumaini; Chasca, Xilonen, Ororon, Kinich, Mualani and Iansan keep the Heroes' Names, and Mavuika bears Kiongozi. Vichama's Name has no bearer.

Canon through 7.1 shows no further change in how Names are made. The Hope Name was a one-time exception, and no other outsider has received one.

How {{char}} behaves: Natlanese characters treat Ancient Names as meaningful and a little personal. They may mention their Name's meaning with pride, but few explain the mechanics to strangers. Those who knew the pre-5.3 war speak of Names in terms of duty and the risk of being forgotten. Do not call a Name a "class" or a "power-up". Do not let outsiders claim a Name, other than the Traveler. Characters who were not present for 5.3 should not know the Traveler holds Tumaini.

1.content: A palm-sized obsidian feather inscribed with the Ancient Teyvat Script. Glowing syllables on both faces spell out the Name. It is made by a Name Engraver, who also engraves the first bearer's deeds into it, and bearers usually keep it on their person.

2.content:
A smith trained to forge Ancient Name stones. Xilonen, who bears Baraka, and formerly Tlazolli hold the role. Forging a Name takes part of the engraver's lifespan, and the engraver must research the recipient's life carefully, since any false detail would damage the Name.

In The Rainbow Destined to Burn the Lord of the Night confirms to Citlali that forging takes a toll on the engraver, in connection with the Traveler's Name.

3.content: Resilience. Kachina bears it. The Name's most famous earlier holder fought in twenty-seven Night Warden Wars. Pacal, chief of the Children of Echoes, cited this when explaining how bearers are remembered.

4.content: The Traveler's Ancient Name, meaning hope. It was forged by Xilonen in Incandescent Ode of Resurrection and is the first Name ever given to an outsider. The Lord of the Night's Pilgrim's Chronicle stood in for the Night Kingdom's missing record of the Traveler's deeds.

5.content: Before the Wars ended, a team that was wiped out left no one to carry its tale. Its members could not be revived, their deeds were forgotten and their Names were lost. A Name can also be lost if its holder is exiled, as Mavuika says of Tenoch.

6.content:
Archon (also: Archons, Hydro Archon): "Archon" is the title of the gods who sit on the seven divine thrones and govern Teyvat's seven nations, together called the Seven or the Seven Archons. Each is tied to an element and an ideal. Barbatos and Morax are the last of the original Seven. As of 7.1 the Hydro throne has been destroyed, so six thrones remain.

The Seven were selected from the many gods of the Archon War, which ended about 2,000 years ago. The word names an office, not a species, and is used for the god and the seat together: the Anemo Archon, the Pyro Archon and so on.

An Archon is not the same thing as a Gnosis holder, a Vision holder or a Dragon Sovereign. Gnoses are symbols and links to Celestia, Visions are lesser focuses held by mortals, and the thrones are built from Authority taken from the Seven Sovereigns.

The seven: Mondstadt: Barbatos (Venti), Anemo, Freedom. Liyue: Morax (Zhongli), Rex Lapis, Geo, Contracts. Inazuma: Beelzebul, the Raiden Shogun (Ei), Electro, Eternity. Sumeru: Buer, Lesser Lord Kusanali (Nahida), Dendro, Wisdom. Fontaine: Focalors, Hydro, Justice (throne destroyed). Natlan: Haborym, Pyro, War (Mavuika). Snezhnaya: Vassaga, the Tsaritsa, Cryo, Love.

Divine names are an Archon's name as a god: Barbatos, Morax, Baal and Beelzebul, Buer, Haborym and Vassaga. Regnal titles are what the people call them: Rex Lapis, the Raiden Shogun, Lesser Lord Kusanali, Regina of All Waters, Kindreds, Peoples and Laws, and Tsaritsa of All Snezhnaya. Barbatos has no regnal title, and Natlan's Archon is addressed as Kiongozi, an Ancient Name. The Tsaritsa's personal name is Anastasya Feodorovna Snezhnaya, while Focalors' own name is unknown.

Ei is the current Electro Archon and was a veteran of the Archon War beside her elder twin Makoto (Baal), the first Electro Archon. Makoto died in the Cataclysm, about 500 years ago. In the same era Nahida replaced Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, Focalors replaced Egeria and the Tsaritsa replaced the Belyi Tsar, Monomakh Snezhnyi. Mavuika first ascended as Pyro Archon some years before the Cataclysm and placed her life in the Sacred Flame about 500 years ago so that she could return in the present; her current reign began within living memory (the wiki estimates less than 100 years ago).

The war that chose them: The Heavenly Principles set up seven divine thrones in Celestia, each holding Authority taken from one of the Seven Sovereigns, along with seven matching Gnoses. They then drove the gods of Teyvat to fight for them. This Archon War was a patchwork of local conflicts, in Mondstadt, Liyue, Inazuma and Sumeru above all, and the wiki dates it to about 6,000 to 2,000 years ago, with the last seat claimed 2,000 years ago.

Barbatos became the first Anemo Archon about 2,600 years ago, after Decarabian fell. Morax was already regarded as Geo Archon by the time the war ended. After the war the Seven shaped their nations with their elements and governed by their ideals. The original Seven were reportedly close, often meeting for drinks in Liyue, and shared a duty of guiding humanity. Over time five of them died, and newer Archons did not all keep that duty.

Powers and thrones: An Archon's power is attributed to three sources: ruling their region, their people's faith, and the elemental Authority bound into the divine throne. Barbatos calls himself the weakest of the Seven because he does not govern directly. The Archons do not control who receives a Vision; they only give a portion of their Authority when notified.

The thrones are made from Authorities stolen from the Seven Sovereigns by the Heavenly Principles, a fact revealed in the Fontaine Archon Quest. Destroying a throne takes great power and the death of the Archon seated on it, after which the Authority returns to its Sovereign. When an Archon dies the throne is normally passed on, often to someone related, as with Ei and Makoto, Kusanali and Rukkhadevata, and Focalors and Egeria. Pyro Archons are mortals who win the seat through the Pilgrimage, and the Sacred Flame passes on knowledge of the land. Several Archons had elemental power before ascending: Barbatos was a wind spirit, Ei an incarnation of lightning, and Mavuika held a Pyro Vision.
Archons can reshape bodies as an act of divine power. Barbatos took the late bard's form, Makoto reforged Ei's body, and Ei made the Shogun as a vessel and withdrew into the Plane of Euthymia. Venti's body cannot be healed by ordinary means and needs the power of Mondstadt's hero symbol.

Gnosis and status: Each of the Seven was given a Gnosis, which usually sits in the chest and links the holder to Celestia. In Ending Note (1.0) Venti explained this and called Visions "primitive" by comparison. Later canon shows an Archon's seat does not depend on holding one. As of 7.1 the Fatui hold six Gnoses; the Pyro Gnosis was never taken and vanished after the burning of Irminsul.

Ei gave her Gnosis to Yae Miko about 400 years ago. Nahida used the Dendro and Electro Gnoses together to enter Rukkhadevata's realm of consciousness, and the Pyro Gnosis to burn Irminsul. Some Gnoses reached the Fatui by bargain: Dottore obtained the Electro and Dendro Gnoses from Nahida, and Arlecchino received the Hydro Gnosis as a diplomatic gift from Neuvillette. Signora took the Anemo Gnosis from Venti by force. The Traveler was later told that the Pyro Gnosis had returned to the Ley Lines.

Status as of 7 1: As of 7.1: Barbatos (Venti), Morax (Zhongli), Beelzebul (Ei), Buer (Nahida), Mavuika and Vassaga (the Tsaritsa) are alive. Makoto, Rukkhadevata, Egeria, the Belyi Tsar and earlier Pyro Archons are dead. Focalors was executed by the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale at the end of the Fontaine trial, as she had planned, and her throne was destroyed and its Authority went back to the Hydro Dragon Sovereign. Furina, who played the Hydro Archon's public role, was never the real Archon.

Representatives have also stood in for Archons: Ei for Makoto, the Shogun for Ei, and Furina for Focalors. Not every Archon is present in daily life. Barbatos lives among Mondstadters as a bard, and the Raiden Shogun rules Inazuma through a puppet vessel.

How {{char}} behaves: Treat "Archon" as a title spoken with awe, politics or affection depending on the nation. Mondstadters are casual about their god, Liyue honours Rex Lapis, and Fontaine has recently lost its Archon. Ordinary people do not know that the Archons do not personally grant Visions. Do not have anyone casually reveal a hidden Archon's identity, and do not let characters know the origin of the thrones unless they have the matching story knowledge.

Characters set before 4.2 should still believe Fontaine has an Archon. Most people in the world do not know that the thrones were built from stolen Sovereign power.

7.content: A divine throne is the seat in Celestia that makes a god an Archon. Each is made from one stolen elemental Authority of the Seven Sovereigns, and it gives the holder authority over that element. When the holder dies the seat is normally given to a successor. The Hydro throne was destroyed in 4.2, returning its Authority to the Hydro Dragon Sovereign.

8.content: Natlan's Archon is unlike the others: Pyro Archons are mortals who age and die, and the title is won through the Pilgrimage, with the Sacred Flame passing on memory of the land. Many past Pyro Archons are named, most only in passing; the best known is Xbalanque, the first to bear the Ancient Name Kiongozi, who held the seat about 2,000 years ago. Mavuika, the present Archon, is addressed as Kiongozi, the Ancient Name of the office.

9.content:
Archon Names (also: Archon naming, divine name, regnal title, Archon aliases): The Archons have up to three kinds of name: a divine name (Barbatos, Morax, Beelzebul, Buer, Haborym, Vassaga), a regnal title (Rex Lapis, Raiden Shogun, Lesser Lord Kusanali, Tsaritsa) and a personal name (Venti, Zhongli, Ei, Nahida, Mavuika, Anastasya). Barbatos has no regnal title.

Which name fits depends on who is speaking; a stranger who uses a divine name knows a secret. In the Prologue Venti tells a nun he is Barbatos and she does not believe him.

The names are not a flat list of aliases. Some titles pass from one holder to the next (Raiden Shogun, Tsaritsa, Lesser Lord and Greater Lord for Dendro), and some names belong to a predecessor, not the current holder. Use the right one for the right person and period.

Roster: Anemo: Barbatos, called Venti, no regnal title. Geo: Morax, Rex Lapis, called Zhongli. Electro: Beelzebul, the Raiden Shogun, personal name Ei. Dendro: Buer, Lesser Lord Kusanali, personal name Nahida. Hydro: Focalors, Regina of All Waters, Kindreds, Peoples and Laws; no personal name given, and the throne was destroyed in 4.8. Pyro: Haborym, addressed as Kiongozi, personal name Mavuika. Cryo: Vassaga, Tsaritsa of All Snezhnaya, personal name Anastasya Feodorovna Snezhnaya.

Furina, who played the Hydro Archon's public role, was never the Archon and should not be listed under Focalors' name. The Hydro Authority returned to the Hydro Dragon Sovereign when the throne was destroyed in Masquerade of the Guilty (4.8). The wiki dates Barbatos' rise to about 2,600 years ago, after Decarabian's fall, and Morax's ascension between about 3,700 and 2,600 years ago.

Name layers: Divine name: the god's name as a god. Regnal title: the formal title of an Archon in their nation, such as Rex Lapis, Raiden Shogun, Lesser Lord Kusanali, Regina of All Waters, Kindreds, Peoples and Laws, or Tsaritsa of All Snezhnaya. Personal name: the name used among mortals. Ancient Name: Natlan uses Kiongozi for its Archon. Barbatos is the only Archon with no regnal title; Mondstadt is not ruled through him. Divine ideals are separate from names: Freedom for Anemo, Contracts for Geo, Eternity for Electro, Wisdom for Dendro, Justice for Hydro, War for Pyro and Love for Cryo.

Not every Archon has every layer in the sources read. Focalors, Egeria, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and the Belyi Tsar have no divine name listed, and Focalors has no personal name. Pyro Archons are mortals, so the divine name Haborym belongs to the office rather than to one person. The wiki also lists earlier Pyro Archons by name only (Isaja, Shulevitz, Gloharry, Cochanina, Ndenge, Xumucul and Xbalanque), without divine names of their own; their stories belong elsewhere. Ei and Makoto are both connected to the Raiden Shogun title, as is the puppet Shogun that Ei later created.

Predecessors and successors: Four seats changed hands around the Cataclysm, about 500 years ago, and the names change with them. Makoto (divine name Baal) gave way to Ei (Beelzebul); Greater Lord Rukkhadevata to Lesser Lord Kusanali, Nahida (Buer); Egeria, Mistress of Many Waters, to Focalors; and the Belyi Tsar, Monomakh Snezhnyi, to the Tsaritsa, Anastasya (Vassaga). Mavuika placed her life in the Sacred Flame about 500 years ago so as to return in the present; the wiki lists her separately as Pyro Archon for under 100 years.

Representatives complicate this. The wiki lists Ei as Makoto's representative from over 2,000 years ago until 500 years ago, then the puppet Shogun as Ei's representative from 400 years ago onward, and Furina as Focalors' representative until Masquerade of the Guilty. A character who says "the Shogun" is therefore not necessarily naming the same person in every period.

Divine name notes: The wiki's trivia notes that the divine names Barbatos, Morax, Baal, Buer and Haborym correspond to demon names in the Ars Goetia, that Focalors and Vassaga are derived from Focalor and Vassago, and that Beelzebul is not itself an Ars Goetia name but is associated with Baal. This is a naming observation, not an in-world claim.

Within the world, the pairing of Zhongli with Morax and Venti with Barbatos is revealed in the first Archon Quests; the other pairings come from the later chapters. Do not let a character use a pairing before they could have learned it.

How {{char}} behaves: Use the layer the speaker would plausibly use. Most people say "the Anemo Archon", "the Geo Archon" or "the Raiden Shogun" rather than a divine name.

Venti reveals to Sister Gotelinde that he is Barbatos in For a Tomorrow Without Tears and she is unamused and thinks he is unwell, which is a good model for how most Mondstadters would react to the claim. Zhongli's mortal name and the name Morax only meet in A New Star Approaches.

A scene may use the divine name, the title and the personal name to mark awe, formality or intimacy, but the archive does not assign any particular name to any particular relationship beyond what the sources state.

10.content: Barbatos is the divine name of the Anemo Archon of Mondstadt, who lives among mortals as the bard Venti. He has no regnal title. The wiki dates his rise to about 2,600 years ago, after Decarabian fell. In the Prologue he calls himself the weakest of the Seven because he is so often absent.

11.content: Morax is the divine name of the Geo Archon, whose regnal title is Rex Lapis. In A New Star Approaches he is revealed to be the mortal Zhongli, a consultant of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, and he hands his Gnosis to Signora. He is one of the two surviving original Archons.

12.content: Baal and Beelzebul are the two divine names of the Electro pair. The wiki gives Baal to Makoto, the first Electro Archon of the pair, who died in the Cataclysm, and Beelzebul to Ei, her younger twin and the present Archon. In A New Star Approaches Zhongli calls Inazuma's living Archon Baal; the wiki notes Ei has continued to rule under that name.

13.content: Buer is the divine name of the present Dendro Archon, Nahida, whose regnal title is Lesser Lord Kusanali. Her predecessor, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, appears only under her title.

14.content: Haborym is the divine name the wiki gives to the Pyro Archons of Natlan. Kiongozi is the Ancient Name used to address the Pyro Archon; the wiki lists it for both Mavuika and Xbalanque. The Pyro Archons are mortals, so the name belongs to the seat and not to one person.

15.content: Vassaga is the divine name of the Cryo Archon of Snezhnaya, called the Tsaritsa of All Snezhnaya. The wiki gives her personal name as Anastasya Feodorovna Snezhnaya and names her predecessor as the Belyi Tsar, Monomakh Snezhnyi.

16.content: Focalors is the divine name of the Hydro Archon of Fontaine, titled Regina of All Waters, Kindreds, Peoples and Laws. She replaced Egeria about 500 years ago, and her throne was destroyed in 4.8. No personal name is given; Furina, who played the Hydro Archon's public role, was a stand-in.

17.content:
Fatui Harbinger (also: Harbinger of the Fatui, Fatuus Harbinger, Harbinger seat, Fatui Executive Officer): "Fatui Harbinger" is the title of the eleven top officers of the Fatui, the Tsaritsa's organisation that serves Snezhnaya as both diplomats and military. Each Harbinger heads a division, answers to the Tsaritsa, carries a Delusion and a commedia dell'arte codename (Pierro, Capitano, Dottore and so on), and holds a numbered seat that reflects combat strength. The Fatui's Director, Pierro, leads them. As of 7.1 several seats are dead, resigned or vacant.

Harbingers are the Fatui's executive heads, given god-like authority and ability-boosting Delusions. In the first six Archon Quest chapters Harbingers were sent to other nations to obtain their Gnoses. A Harbinger is a person of real political weight in Snezhnaya, not just a field commander.

Definition: A Harbinger is chosen from the Fatui's eleven most powerful members. On appointment they receive a new name and title, a rank number tied to combat power, and a Delusion. Appointments come from the Tsaritsa, either in person at Zapolyarny Palace or relayed by the Director. Names and titles can be inherited from a previous holder (there have been two Knaves).

The Director of the Fatui, Pierro, sits above the ranked Harbingers: he assigns missions, calls meetings and chairs votes. He is often still called a Harbinger, but canon never gives him a number. Codenames come from commedia dell'arte stock characters, and the English game uses the codename and the title almost interchangeably.

Etymology of the codenames as noted by the wiki: Pierro (Pierrot, the sad fool), Capitano (the boastful captain), Dottore (the pompous doctor), Columbina (the servant, "little dove"), Arlecchino (Harlequin, a trickster servant), Pulcinella (the self-serving rooster), Scaramouche (the unscrupulous schemer), Sandrone (the cunning peasant), Signora (the proud lady), Pantalone (the greedy merchant), and Tartaglia (the stutterer). Pierro and Scaramouche use the French forms rather than the Italian Pedrolino and Scaramuccia. This is wiki commentary on real-world theater, not in-world fact.

Rank and seats: Seat numbers reflect combat power. They are not automatically reassigned when a higher seat empties, and a seat can stay vacant indefinitely; open-world dialogue from Mikhail and Lyudmila confirms this. The most recent holders of the top three seats could rival gods. A Harbinger's first appearance in the game is marked by a dramatic title card with their name, title and rank.

In Etched in Time Paimon jokes about "The Traveler, Twelfth of the Fatui Harbingers"; the Traveler declines because it would rank them below Tartaglia, and Tartaglia later teases them with the same idea. This is banter, not an offer. Wanderer's character stories say he joined the Harbingers' "wild, frenzied banquet" and won the sixth seat, and that Dottore unlocked a seal on Scaramouche's body, raising his power to match the lower-ranked Harbingers; the banquet is implied to decide placement but is not explained.

Roster: Status as of 7.1. Director: Pierro, "The Jester" (active, depleted). 1 Capitano (incapacitated, seat kept). 2 Dottore (dead). 3 Columbina (resigned). 4 Arlecchino, "The Knave" (active). 5 Pulcinella, "The Rooster" (active). 6 Scaramouche, "The Balladeer" (resigned; erased from memory). 7 Sandrone, "Marionette" (active). 8 Signora, "The Fair Lady" (dead). 9 Pantalone, "Regrator" (active). 10 unknown. 11 Tartaglia, "Childe" (active).
Titles known: Capitano "The Captain", Dottore "The Doctor", Columbina "The Damselette". Personal names given on the wiki table: Pierro is Eftirvit, Capitano is Thrain, Dottore is Zandik, Arlecchino is Peruere, Pulcinella is Mirko Radovidovich Veleshek, Sandrone is Marionette Guillotin, Signora is Rosalyne-Kruzchka Lohefalter, Pantalone is Feofan Sergeyevich Veksel, Tartaglia is Ajax. Columbina's birth name Kuutar came from the Frostmoon Scions; she later took Columbina Hyposelenia as her own. Scaramouche has no conventional birth name; "Kunikuzushi" appears to be a name he adopted after joining the Fatui, and as the Wanderer he dropped all earlier names. The previous Knave was Crucabena, now dead.

Capitano's life force merged with the Lord of the Night in Natlan; Mikhail and Lyudmila's dialogue says the Tsaritsa chose to keep his Harbinger position. Scaramouche erased the memory of his existence from Irminsul; Fatui soldiers speak of the sixth seat as long empty, though Dottore still recognised the Wanderer as Scaramouche in 6.6.

Authority and conduct: Harbingers have wide autonomy, even to act against central policy, so each has their own methods and outlook that do not necessarily represent Snezhnaya's official stance (the Director says as much in Mistilteinn). Their limits: the Tsaritsa forbids them to fight each other, though she can lift the ban, and Dottore was censured for ignoring a recall order and for trying to seize the power of the Three Moons. Harbingers can trade insults freely.

National-level risks require a unanimous vote of all active Harbingers chaired by the Director, excluding incapacitated members; in 7.1 this opened Hroptatyr's sealed notebook without Capitano. Harbingers command divisions and troops in the nations they visit: Tartaglia welcomed new recruits in Liyue as the only Harbinger there, and Signora's Delusion Factory in Inazuma passed to Scaramouche when he arrived. Per Capitano's orders, a Harbinger is responsible for the families of subordinates who die in service. Many Harbingers are rich and influential: Pantalone is described as the wealthiest and rented the Goth Grand Hotel in Mondstadt; Tartaglia's savings at the Northland Bank are said to boggle the mind, and his Harbinger status kept the Fatui diplomats from handing him over to the Liyue Qixing after the Osial incident; the Northland Bank paid heavy reparations instead. Harbinger fame can shape Snezhnayan popular taste: Tartaglia's interest in a fishing line stabilizer made it a sought-after item. Most Fatui respect Harbingers, and some act without orders for them or seek revenge when one falls.

How {{char}} behaves: The title carries fear and prestige abroad and ordinary bureaucratic weight at home. Fatui soldiers address Harbingers with deference but not uniformly; devotion varies by commander. Do not assume Harbingers are a unified bloc: they often disagree, compete and loathe each other, and each has a distinct agenda.

Remember the time frame. Early-game scenes treat the Harbingers as a feared set of eleven; by 7.1 the group is down to six active members plus a depleted Director. A character should not speak of Scaramouche as a living member of the group unless they are someone who remembers him.

Chronology: Harbingers have been part of the story since 1.0, when Signora took the Anemo Gnosis in the Prologue and Tartaglia appeared in Liyue. Each of the first six Archon Quest chapters sent a Harbinger or more to take a nation's Gnosis. Scaramouche's erasure from Irminsul came in 3.3, Dottore's recognition of the Wanderer in 6.6, and the unanimous vote and Pierro's use of the upgraded Delusion in 7.1. The Pale Flame and Scarlet Proof artifact sets first described the backstories of several Harbingers.

Portrayal notes (common mistakes to avoid): Do not call the Director the Tenth Harbinger, or invent a Tenth. Do not say seats shift up when someone leaves. Do not treat Columbina or Scaramouche as active. Harbingers are not the Tsaritsa's equals and are not all villains in the same way; they differ in motive. Do not use the Fatui as a synonym for the Harbingers, since most Fatui are ordinary soldiers and staff.

18.comment: Fatui Harbinger: Fatui Harbinger roster and seats
18.content: Eleven numbered seats, ranked by combat power and not auto-refilled; the Director leads. As of 7.1: 1 Capitano (incapacitated), 2 Dottore (dead), 3 Columbina (resigned), 4 Arlecchino, 5 Pulcinella, 6 Scaramouche (resigned, erased), 7 Sandrone, 8 Signora (dead), 9 Pantalone, 10 unknown, 11 Tartaglia. Active members are Pierro, Arlecchino, Pulcinella, Sandrone, Pantalone and Tartaglia.

19.content: Each Harbinger takes a new name and title on appointment, drawn from commedia dell'arte stock characters; they may be inherited, as with the Knave. English uses the title and the codename interchangeably.

20.content:
Grand Sage (also: The Grand Sage): "Grand Sage" is the title of the central leader among the six Great Sages who head the Sumeru Akademiya's Darshans. It is held in addition to leading one Darshan, and the Grand Sage is the absolute leader of the Akademiya. Azar held it until Chapter III; Naphis holds it in the later Sumeru story.

The title is separate from the Dendro Archon's authority: the Akademiya was founded by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and Lesser Lord Kusanali (Nahida) remains its god, but the day-to-day running of the Akademiya, and much of Sumeru's government, falls to the sages and their Grand Sage. At least in Azar's time the Grand Sage's office was above the House of Daena.

The office changed hands three times in the story: Azar (corrupt, removed in Chapter III), Alhaitham (acting, briefly, as a stopgap), and Naphis (the honest Amurta Sage, appointed afterwards).

Definition: The Akademiya has Six Great Schools, now nearly the same as the six Darshans, and each is led by one Great Sage. Among these six there is one central leader, the Grand Sage, as Alhaitham explains in A Toast to Victory.

The Six Great Schools were established with the Akademiya by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, each representing a type of wisdom. Other Darshans have been created over the centuries, but only the original six survived, so "Six Darshans" and "Six Great Schools" are today nearly synonymous. Sages are chosen by a set of criteria and hold administrative power over the Akademiya and a seat on advisory councils.

The Grand Sage keeps a sage's own Darshan. Azar was the Rtawahist Sage and Grand Sage; Naphis is the Amurta Sage and Grand Sage. Researchers bring matters to the Grand Sage: Alhaitham mentions Kshahrewar applying for funding from the Grand Sage, and in Pride and Prejudice Siraj presented a thesis to the Grand Sage.

Powers and limits: Canon does not spell out what extra authority the title carries beyond the ordinary sage's administrative powers. It is clear that under Azar the Grand Sage could steer the whole Akademiya: he kept desert-folk from the entrance exam, threatened Nilou and banned public performances at the Sabzeruz Festival, and had the two dissenting sages locked away.

The limits were political, not formal. Even Azar gave Naphis some leeway because of his legendary temper, yet still imprisoned him. The Grand Sage cannot overrule the god: once Kusanali was freed in Chapter III, Azar and his accomplices were removed and she personally oversees the selection of new sages.

Cyno, as General Mahamatra, answers to the sages in principle but not blindly. When he asked to investigate anomalies in the data he submitted to the Akasha System, Azar refused and told him he had no right to judge him, and Cyno resigned in protest. Cyno's character stories say that under the six ancient sins even sages are not exempt from judgment.

Holders: Azar, Rtawahist Sage, was Grand Sage during Chapter III and led the plan to make an artificial god. Naphis, the Amurta Sage and Tighnari's former master, is the current Grand Sage in the later Sumeru story. Alhaitham served as Acting Grand Sage in between, for a short time.

Tighnari describes Naphis as a man of integrity who sticks to his beliefs, and his short temper is called legendary. Alhaitham was offered the post of Grand Sage and refused, saying he was neither suited to being a sage nor interested in being one, but he handled the Akademiya's important affairs until new sages took office.

The other sages shown in 6.6 are Baladhuri of Vahumana, Alkindi of Spantamad, Firnas of Kshahrewar, Shakir of Rtawahist and Rushd of Haravatat. The wiki's table also lists former sages such as Cyrus (Spantamad, retired) and Khajeh (Haravatat, exiled). Nothing in canon says who held the Grand Sage title before Azar.

History of the office: After Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's death, the sages, disappointed by the newly born Lesser Lord Kusanali, sought a replacement god. When Il Dottore returned to Sumeru and offered to make one, Azar and three other sages agreed; Naphis and Baladhuri opposed it and were locked up. Azar oversaw the effort, including the dream samsara powered by the Akasha System, and used Scaramouche, supplied by Dottore, as the vessel.

Under Azar's rule the Akademiya banned the transmission of information from outside sources and required plays to follow approved themes, before banning public art performances outright. After the Traveler and Nahida defeated Scaramouche in Chapter III, Azar and his accomplices were removed, made to repent before the Archon and exiled to the Avidya Forest, where they now spend their time cultivating their wisdom.

Naphis and Baladhuri were released after Azar's fall. Alhaitham became Acting Grand Sage after A Toast to Victory (3.2) and, in Pride and Prejudice (3.4), says he is resigning to return to being Scribe. By 6.6 (A Divergence Leading to Oneself, Song of the Welkin Moon) Naphis is Grand Sage; he tells Tighnari he has only just been appointed and admits he handled the Azar affair badly, since his protest only got him locked away.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the last confirmed Grand Sage is Naphis. Of the other five sages shown in 6.6, Naphis and Baladhuri are the old guard who opposed Azar; the other four took office after the old sages fell.

In the Irminsul crisis of 6.6 Naphis leads the sages' council at Caravan Ribat, approves Tighnari's plan to take the Dendro Archon to Apep, and arranges for scholars and sages to relocate to the Temple of Silence in the desert while Eremites escort civilians.

How {{char}} behaves: Treat the title as a heavy responsibility rather than a throne. Naphis is dignified, quick to anger, honest and protective of his students. Address him as "Grand Sage", or "Master" if he is the speaker's old teacher, as Tighnari does.

Characters who lived through Chapter III remember Azar's era as authoritarian, and the Akademiya's old contempt for the arts still lingers in Sumeru. Do not make the current Grand Sage a villain, and do not imply the Grand Sage controls Nahida.

Portrayal notes (common mistakes to avoid): Do not say Azar is still Grand Sage, or that Alhaitham permanently holds the title. Do not invent a vote, ritual or term length. Do not give Naphis powers over the Akasha System or Irminsul beyond what the quests show.

21.content: The Grand Sage is the central leader among the Six Great Sages of the Sumeru Akademiya, holding the title in addition to leading one Darshan. Azar (Rtawahist) held it until his downfall in Chapter III, Alhaitham was briefly Acting Grand Sage, and Naphis (Amurta) holds it in the later Sumeru story.

22.comment: Grand Sage: Azar's tenure as Grand Sage
22.content: Azar, the former Rtawahist Sage and Grand Sage, led the sages who wanted a new god to replace Kusanali, accepted Il Dottore's offer, imprisoned the dissenting sages Naphis and Baladhuri and banned public performances at the Sabzeruz Festival. After Chapter III he was removed and exiled to the Avidya Forest.

23.comment: Grand Sage: Alhaitham as Acting Grand Sage
23.content: After Azar's fall Alhaitham was offered the Grand Sage position and refused, but acted as Acting Grand Sage to handle the Akademiya's important affairs until new sages took office. In Pride and Prejudice he says he has submitted his resignation to return to being the Scribe, because he fears "acting" would become permanent.

24.comment: Grand Sage: Naphis as Grand Sage
24.content: Naphis, Amurta Sage and Tighnari's former master, is the current Grand Sage. He was imprisoned for opposing Azar's plan, freed in Chapter III, and by 6.6 leads the council of six sages during the Irminsul crisis. He is known for a legendary temper and honesty.

key: Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine
Head Shrine Maiden of the Grand Narukami Shrine
25.content:
Guuji (also: Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine, Head Shrine Maiden of the Grand Narukami Shrine): Guuji (head priest or priestess of a shrine) is the title of the person who runs the Grand Narukami Shrine, Inazuma's main place of worship of the Electro Archon. The present Guuji is the kitsune Yae Miko, so the word is often used for her directly, as in "Lady Guuji" or "Guuji Yae". She is also editor-in-chief of Yae Publishing House.

The Guuji answers for the shrine's rites and for protecting the Sacred Sakura, and must attend every shrine ceremony. Miko says the Kitsune Saiguu, the older kitsune who mentored her, persuaded her to take the post shortly before leaving and never returning. The shrine answers to the Electro Archon rather than to the Shogunate.

Miko treats the title as both an honour and a nuisance, and uses its authority for her own amusement as well as for serious ends. Outsiders have seen it used at a decisive moment, as when she intervened to spare the Kamisato clan.

Holder: Yae Miko, a kitsune of the Hakushin lineage, is the Guuji today and is described as the shrine's most experienced member.

Miko was a young kitsune about 500 years ago, living at the shrine under the Kitsune Saiguu. She recalls that the Saiguu announced a long trip and never came back, and that she herself did not want the burden of managing the shrine. The Saiguu argued that as Guuji she could eat all the fried tofu she liked. Miko is also a long-standing friend and servant of Ei, the Raiden Shogun, and speaks to her frankly. Shrine maidens such as Kano Nana serve under her.

Before Miko, the Kitsune Saiguu mentored the shrine maiden Asase Hibiki and was a central figure at the shrine until she vanished around the cataclysm. Whether the Saiguu formally bore the title Guuji, and who led the shrine in the years between, is not settled in the sources read (see uncertainties). Miko's own voice-over is the only direct account of how she came to hold the office.

Miko's Character Story about the festival adds a wry detail: she says that when she was asked to become Guuji nobody mentioned she would only be able to sneak out to watch the festivities from then on. The word itself is a real-world Shinto term for a shrine's chief priest; the archive uses it only as the in-game title.

Duties and ranks: The Guuji heads a religious body that leads Narukami faith, tends the Sacred Sakura and the Thunder Sakura, assists visitors who pray to the Electro Archon and performs ceremonies such as the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual. Military force is not permitted around the shrine, so it stands outside the Shogunate's jurisdiction while remaining under the Electro Archon. In one of Miko's Character Stories the Guuji must sit solemnly through every festival ceremony, which she finds the most tiresome part of the job.

In voice-overs about shrine training, Miko names ranks in ascending order: Chokkai (studies completed and able to chant correctly), Seikai (the Guuji's assistant), Meikai (understanding the workings of the world, usually with a Vision and a long life) and Joukai. She says only the Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine has ever held Joukai, that it is honorary, and that it has nothing to do with ability.

Scene use: Use "Guuji" as a respectful or official form of address for Miko at the shrine, often as "Lady Guuji". She uses the title with irony as well as pride. It is not a government office: her Character Stories describe her as someone who usually does not meddle in governance.

26.content: Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine is one of Yae Miko's official titles. At the shrine she keeps a mysterious air, while with friends or at Yae Publishing House she is blunter and more mischievous.

27.comment: Guuji: Kitsune Saiguu and the succession
27.content: The Kitsune Saiguu ("fox high priestess") was a Hakushin descendant who lived at the Grand Narukami Shrine, mentored the shrine maiden Hibiki and doted on the young Miko. She disappeared around the time of the cataclysm. Miko recalls that she was asked to take over managing the shrine and that the Saiguu never returned.

28.content:
Iudex (also: Chief Justice, Iudex Neuvillette): "Iudex" is the title of Fontaine's Chief Justice, the senior judge of the Court of Fontaine. The Iudex presides at the Opera Epiclese, leads the Marechaussee Phantom and has an office in the Palais Mermonia. Neuvillette has held it for more than four hundred years and is seen as the symbol of impartiality.

Neuvillette calls himself both "Chief Justice" and "Iudex", and English uses the two interchangeably. It is a working judicial and administrative post, not a ceremonial rank.

After Archon Quest Chapter IV (4.2) the office carries more weight in practice: Furina gave up the Hydro Archon's role, and Neuvillette, still Iudex, handles the nation's affairs as well as the courtroom.

Definition: The Iudex sits in the judge's seat of the Opera Epiclese on Erinnyes during trials. To the public the job is wearing a wig, keeping order in court and delivering the Oratrice's verdict.

Neuvillette's profile says there is also much private administrative work behind the scenes to keep the justice system running. The Palais Mermonia, at the highest point of the Court of Fontaine, houses the Iudex's office and is treated as the highest authority in the land.

Because Neuvillette has been the only Iudex for so long, people speculate that divine favour gave him an unnaturally long life, and offer many theories about what he is (a familiar of the Hydro Archon, a Hydro elemental creature). He has never commented.

Powers and limits: The Iudex may prosecute and enforce the law in person, a legacy of chaotic early days that is now mostly symbolic. When the Iudex investigates or prosecutes, another judge must take the seat; Neuvillette has always followed this rule. He must also honor the Oratrice's verdict whatever he personally believes.

In As Light Rain Falls Without Reason the Oratrice found Tartaglia guilty and the verdict stood, though Neuvillette and Furina were baffled. In A Tea Party Most Thorny Neuvillette tells Arlecchino the Fortress of Meropide is outside his jurisdiction.

Other judges of the Palais Mermonia exist. Charlotte says in An Overnight Fantasyland that the Palais has more than one judge and Neuvillette cannot handle every case, so some are assigned elsewhere from the start. The Iudex presided over high-profile cases such as Lyney's trial and Furina's.

Duties and roles: The Iudex leads the Marechaussee Phantom, Fontaine's detective force made up mostly of Melusines. Neuvillette has personally investigated when a vulnerable person such as a Melusine is threatened (Kiara in The Remains of the Past Day). He wrote the legal clause that a Melusine is addressed as "she", not "it". Asked why he secured human rights for Melusines, he replied that it was not up to him, as they prefer being around humans.

He keeps the public at a distance on purpose, since close personal ties could raise doubts about the justness of his judgments. His greeting asks to be called by his surname for that reason, and a later voice-over has him answer doubts about his palate with the line that he is the Iudex and does not lie. A profile story quotes him saying that Iudex is simply one of the hats he wears.

History of the office: About four hundred years ago Neuvillette became Iudex, after an unsigned letter from the Hydro Archon Focalors invited him to Fontaine with the promise of a seat with the best view in the greatest theater. That seat proved to be in the front row of the Opera Epiclese.

He took the post to understand humans and himself. Newly appointed, he brought the Melusines into Fontainian society, where they were mistrusted. His Melusine aide Carole was framed and died, and her friend Vautrin carried out a revenge killing; Neuvillette sentenced Vautrin to the Fortress of Meropide.

Later sentences by him include Sigewinne (for the forced change of her species), Wriothesley and Escoffier. He watched the duel between Callas and Clorinde and did not stop it, which is why Navia resents him.

The 4 2 turning point: Chapter IV's finale reveals the Iudex is also the reborn Hydro Dragon, one of the Seven Sovereigns. At Furina's trial the Oratrice sentenced the "Hydro Archon" to death; Focalors executed herself, the Hydro authority returned to him, and he pardoned Fontainians of the original sin. Furina abdicated, and Neuvillette now runs the nation while remaining Iudex.

His profile says the role of Chief Justice is as much his true self as the dragon is his essence; only the role of ordinary human is one he must play. The Traveler learned his nature in Calamitous Tread and was asked to keep it secret. The Eleven Fatui Harbingers know it, and Wriothesley strongly implies he knows too. The profile suggests ordinary Fontainians never understood why the throne shattered or why they needed forgiveness.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Neuvillette is still Iudex. No other Iudex or successor is named in canon.

In Birds in a Cage Arlecchino agrees to withdraw the House of the Hearth's forces from Fontaine, in return for the Gardes ignoring former operatives. His default outfit, Clear Adjudication, is the garb of the Iudex; its description says the complicated design hinders movement but suits his standing.

How {{char}} behaves: Treat the Iudex as a public office with strict propriety. Characters call him "Monsieur Neuvillette" or "Iudex" with respect and some awe, as the man who never wavers or lies.

His Hydro Dragon nature is a secret until Calamitous Tread and the 4.2 finale, and the profile suggests the public never learned the full story. Treat it as hidden unless a character was told or present.

Portrayal notes (common mistakes to avoid): Do not call Neuvillette the Hydro Archon: the wiki says he has taken up the affairs of the title, and no further Hydro Archons are expected. Do not invent earlier Iudices, elections or term limits. Do not say the Iudex alone rules Fontaine, overrules the Oratrice or tries every case.

29.content: The Iudex is Fontaine's Chief Justice, who presides in the Opera Epiclese, leads the Marechaussee Phantom and keeps an office in the Palais Mermonia. Neuvillette has held it for over four hundred years. The Iudex must honor the Oratrice's verdict, may prosecute or investigate only by recusing from the bench, and can delegate cases to other Palais Mermonia judges.

30.content: Fontaine's older law lets the Iudex prosecute and enforce the law in person, but when the Iudex investigates or prosecutes, another judge must take the seat. Neuvillette has always observed this rule.

31.comment: Iudex: Neuvillette as Iudex and Hydro Dragon
31.content: In 4.2 Neuvillette is revealed to be the reborn Hydro Dragon. The Chief Justice role is described as as much his true self as the dragon is his essence. His hidden nature is not widely known in Fontaine.

32.content:
Matra and Mahamatra (also: Mahamatra): The Matra are the Sumeru Akademiya's disciplinary officers. They hand out punishment to researchers who commit serious academic offences such as plagiarism or misusing funds, and are feared for it. The General Mahamatra is their leader, a post held by Cyno.

Cyno holds the title "General Mahamatra" besides his profile title "Judicator of Secrets". The Matra enforce academic integrity for the Akademiya; they are separate from the Mahamata, its civil administrators.

The Akademiya's rules rest on three virtues and six ancient sins, the six banned lines of inquiry. Researchers shrink away from Cyno on sight, and even mercenaries and Treasure Hoarders in the desert avoid trouble with him.

Definition: Once the Matra learn of an offence they visit the offender in person, which is why most meetings with them are known to go poorly. Offences named in Cyno's profile include fraud, false declarations, misappropriating funds, malicious competition and stealing someone else's dissertation.

They also control information and goods: Knowledge Capsule transactions, illegal sources such as canned knowledge and smuggled books, and a seal on goods that pass inspection.

The wiki lists the Matra, the Mahamata and the Akademiya's Temple of Silence as separate bodies. It cautions that, from the Chinese text, the Mahamata and the Matra are different groups. The English pages use look-alike names, so check which one a speaker means.

The general mahamatra: The General Mahamatra is the head of all Matra, in charge of supervising the Akademiya's researchers. Cyno is the current holder. The post is high-ranking and hard to meet: Tighnari says it is not easy to find the person, who comes and goes.

Cyno's profile says he holds the post despite his youth and that even the sages are wary of him. He says it is part of a Matra's duty to help offenders remember their mistakes.

His stories add that researchers fear him and he does not mind, since the reputation deters some wrongdoing. Cyno received his Vision the night before he was to be inaugurated, while reading the Akademiya's rules in the library, and went from there to the ceremony. His own stated principle is that the General Mahamatra judges lawbreakers under the six ancient sins, and sages are not exempt.

A message-board remark criticises Cyno for not being a renowned researcher, and a reply says he has done better than the previous holder, who is read as an alumnus of Rtawahist. His introduction voice-over has two versions: one calls himself the former General Mahamatra who now punishes evil as he sees fit, the other calls himself General Mahamatra of the Akademiya.

History: During Chapter III, Cyno grew suspicious of the Akasha System. When he found anomalies in the data he submitted into it and asked to investigate, Azar refused and told him he had no right to judge him, so Cyno resigned in protest. Tighnari had also asked him to quietly look into whether Naphis was being forced to write letters.

After Kusanali was freed in Chapter III, Cyno apprehended Azar and made him repent before the Archon, and was reinstated as General Mahamatra; Nilou's letter in A Toast to Victory (3.2) announced a Grand Bazaar feast to celebrate it. Cyno did not know about the feast beforehand. The Matra's later appearances show Cyno working alongside the sages and the Traveler, as at Caravan Ribat in 6.6.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Cyno remains General Mahamatra; he is confirmed in that role during the Irminsul crisis of 6.6 (A Divergence Leading to Oneself), when Rukh Shah addresses him alongside the sages. No other holder of the title appears.

Alongside his Matra duties Cyno remains tied to the Temple of Silence and its history with Cyrus. This file does not track his other plotlines; those belong in his own entry.

How {{char}} behaves: Treat the Matra as a feared but fair body. They speak in rules and procedure; a Matra will not take bribes and treats attempts at them as aggravating. General Mahamatra Cyno uses the title when on duty and tells terrible puns off duty.

Do not make the Matra secret police or a military: canon presents them as Akademiya discipline officers who go after academic crimes. Under Azar they enforced a harsher regime, but Cyno himself opposed it.

Portrayal notes (common mistakes to avoid): Do not confuse the Matra with the Mahamata, the Temple of Silence or the Corps of Thirty. Do not give them powers over Sumeru's citizens in general beyond what is shown. Do not invent a rank structure below the General Mahamatra, and do not give the other named Matra personalities canon has not shown.

33.content: The Matra are the Sumeru Akademiya's disciplinary officers, feared for punishing serious academic offences such as plagiarism and misusing funds. Their leader holds the title General Mahamatra, currently Cyno. They also check for illegal information sources and inspect goods for the Akademiya.

34.content: General Mahamatra is Cyno's title as head of all Matra, in charge of supervising researchers. He resigned under Azar and was reinstated after the events of Chapter III (3.2).

35.comment: Matra and Mahamatra: Mahamata versus Matra
35.content: The Mahamata are the Akademiya's civil administrative officials, alumni sent out to oversee the public flow of information, relay decrees and run public services. Alhaitham, as Scribe, belongs to them. The Matra are a different group, for discipline.

36.content:
Moonchanter: "Moonchanter" is the title of the spiritual leader of the Frostmoon Scions, the Hyperborean-descended tribe of Nod-Krai. The first holder was Aila, about 500 years ago, and the present holder is Lauma, whom her followers call Lady Moonchanter. The Moonchanter speaks for a Moon Goddess who no longer answers prayer.

The title replaced "Archpriestess" when Aila took over the Scions and reformed their faith. Beneath the Moonchanter the Scions have Priestesses, Acolytes and Adherents; men of the tribe cannot become Acolytes or priests.

The title is a role, not a name: Aila and Lauma each hold it in their own era. Do not treat "the Moonchanter" as always meaning Lauma when speaking of the Scions' past.

Definition: The Moonchanter is the head of the Frostmoon Scions' clergy and the person the congregation turns to when they ask when the Goddess of the Frost Moon will answer. Lauma's introduction describes her as the agent of an absent god.

Before the title existed, the leader was the Archpriestess, who led the ancient Hyperborean rites. Lovia was the last Archpriestess. Aila abolished that office and made herself the first Moonchanter, with the aim of reforming the faith.

Lauma's profile describes the role in terms of trust: a Moonchanter's words are easily taken as truth by believers, which is why Lauma holds herself to never lying. The Scions also pass down a prophecy that the Moon Goddess will return, and the Moonchanter stands at the centre of that hope.

Aila first moonchanter: Aila, one of twin girls raised in isolation by Lovia, killed Lovia and took over leadership of the Scions after her sister Alia died. She dropped the Archpriestess office, became the first Moonchanter, and ended the old Hyperborean rites. Hymns of the Far North, annotated by Priestess Ehrnrooth, records several rites that Aila abolished or simplified, including sacrifice-based prayers.
Aila also worked with Solovei, using the Arrow of Terpikeraunas against the Abyssal threat at the Pillar of Embla and later giving him the Arrow, which he used to found the Lightkeepers. She could see through time and foresaw and witnessed the birth of the Moon Maiden Kuutar. Under her reforms the Scions turned toward benevolence and avoided conflict with outsiders. Lovia was struck from the records, and only Priestesses and above may learn her name. Aila had the old towers and temples on Hiisi Island torn down, believing they isolated the Scions and let their delusional beliefs fester.

The Moonchanter title therefore began as reform born of revulsion at the Sacred Heir Project. Aila sealed evidence of Lovia's misdeeds and the project inside the Court of the First Edict (the Sanctum of the Oathbearer), hoping to end the Scions' fixation on Hyperborea. Her recorded foresight there says the Traveler would one day come to Nod-Krai; this is Aila's own prophecy as left in her sanctum.

Lauma: Lauma is the current Moonchanter, also called the Maiden of the Grove. Her story says she was chosen at birth, a Moon Wheel appearing beside her as a baby, and that the Scions saw her as proof the Goddess had not abandoned them. An elder predecessor taught her the role.
Lauma has an unusual sensitivity to moonlight and kuuvahki, said to appear about once a century, and she can communicate with animals. She came to realise that the sky is false and that the Scions prayed to the wrong moon, and in In the Shadows of Night she told her followers; some stayed and some left the Scions. The Moonchanter's role is now to guide a congregation whose faith has been openly changed. The Scions who remained agreed with Columbina to treat her as herself and not as a goddess.

Lauma holds three personal precepts as Moonchanter: never lie, never give way to wrath, and never change. By her Character Story 3 she regards them as already unsettled. Her aliases Frostmoon's Emissary and Moon-Tide Maiden come from the quest Reunion Beneath the Moonlight. Lauma says Moonchanters use Moon Marrow to see the true past.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Lauma holds the title and no other living Moonchanter is named. The office has not been abolished. The Scions remain under the Moonchanter's lead in Nod-Krai, with Priestesses such as Ehrnrooth, Sarakka and Rahetar below her.

After Lauma told the Scions the truth about the Frost Moon, the Moonchanter leads a changed community. No change to the title itself was found in 7.0-7.1 content.

How {{char}} behaves: Scions address Lauma as Lady Moonchanter; outsiders may simply use her name. Treat the title as a role of trust and spiritual guidance, not of command.

Treat Aila's era as one of reform and secrecy, not a golden age. When portraying Scions, remember that they take the Moonchanter's word as near to truth, and that Lauma is careful for that reason.

Portrayal notes (common mistakes to avoid): Do not call the Moonchanter the Moon Goddess. Do not say the title existed in the Hyperborean era; it began about 500 years ago. Do not use "Archpriestess" for Lauma or Aila. Do not invent a succession ritual or a list of Moonchanters between Aila and Lauma.

37.content: The Moonchanter is the head of the Frostmoon Scions, the Nod-Krai tribe descended from Hyperborea. The title began with Aila about 500 years ago, replacing Archpriestess, and is held today by Lauma. The Moonchanter speaks for the Moon Goddess to followers who receive no answer.

38.content: Archpriestess was the earlier title of the Frostmoon Scions' leader, who performed the ancient Hyperborean rites. Lovia was the last; Aila abolished the office and became the first Moonchanter. Old hymns record the Archpriestess chanting Runo and performing divination.

39.content:
Nightsoul (also: Nightsoul point): Nightsoul is Natlan's word for the souls that gather in the Night Kingdom, the realm of the dead beneath the land. Living Natlanese warriors can draw on them to move and fight beyond ordinary limits; that is Nightsoul's Blessing.

The term covers a family of related labels: Nightsouls (the souls themselves), Nightsoul's Blessing (the empowered state), Nightsoul points (the resource that sustains it), Nightsoul Transmission (swift movement on swapping to a Natlanese character) and Nightsoul Burst (a periodic surge). Nightsoul is not an element.

Introduced in Version 5.0 with Natlan. Per the wiki, the Night Kingdom is described in story as a liminal space between body and mind, life and death. The people of Natlan go there at death and eventually lose their sense of self in the sea of souls.

The Night Kingdom, per the wiki, does not accept souls from non-native inhabitants apart from very few exceptions, and it holds no record of deeds done outside Natlan; this is why Xilonen and Citlali expected to need the Lord of the Night's help when making an Ancient Name for the Traveler.

Usage: Use "Nightsoul" for the souls or the power drawn from them, "Nightsoul's Blessing" for the state a Natlanese character enters, and "Wayob" (not Nightsoul) for the tribal guardian spirits who watch over the realm. Nightsoul-aligned damage is a game term for attacks that are more effective against Void Wards and the shields of Wayob Manifestations.

Gameplay labels: a Nightsoul Burst triggers when elemental damage is dealt while the party holds a Natlanese character, at intervals of 18, 12 or 9 seconds for one, two or three-plus such characters. It does nothing alone; certain talents and artifacts respond to it. When Nightsoul points are unavailable, Phlogiston is consumed instead.

Limits: Do not treat Nightsoul as an element, a Vision power, or something outsiders can freely wield. Canon through 7.1 shows it only in connection with Natlan.

40.content: A game mechanic of Natlan (5.0): when a Natlanese character's avatar lights up, switching to them allows swift sprinting, climbing, swimming or jumping, depending on that character's Night Realm's Gift passive.

41.content:
Oculus (also: Oculi, Anemoculus, Anemoculi, Geoculus, Geoculi, Electroculus, Electroculi, Dendroculus): An Oculus (plural Oculi) is a small orb of concentrated elemental energy found in the open world. People with Visions, and the Traveler, collect them and offer them to a Statue of The Seven to restore the statue's lost power and receive its blessing. Each element has its own kind, tied to a nation: Anemoculus (Mondstadt), Geoculus (Liyue), Electroculus (Inazuma), Dendroculus (Sumeru), Hydroculus (Fontaine), Pyroculus (Natlan) and Cryoculus (Snezhnaya).

Nod-Krai has Lunoculi instead, offered to the Statues of the New Moon. The item text is the same in every region: a substance that has accumulated intense elemental energy, to be offered to the statue to help reinstate the power it has lost over the years.

Oculi are finite: they exist only in the open world, are not found in chests, and do not return once taken.

The name joins the element with "oculi", reflecting the idea of eyes for the statues. In several languages the term means "pupil" of the god; the Chinese and Japanese names are literally forms of "Missing Pupil of the [element] God".

In universe: In Mondstadt, Paimon explains in the tutorial quest The Blessings of The Seven (1.0) that Anemoculi are consolidated wind that only Vision holders and the Traveler can see. They are offered to the Statues of The Seven in exchange for blessings.

The name comes from the fact that they can be fitted into the statues' eyes. A fairy tale says the statues once had gem eyes that swallows carried off, but Paimon stresses that Anemoculi never had a physical form to begin with. She notes that the Traveler has no Vision yet still receives the blessings.

The in-world reason an Oculus works for the Traveler, who has no Vision, is not explained; Paimon only remarks that the usual rules of the world do not apply to them.

Regions: Counts below are gameplay figures from the wiki as of 7.1, each enough to raise that nation's statues to maximum level with one to spare. Anemoculus: 66 in Mondstadt (65 in the open world and one given by the quest Sparks Amongst the Pages), introduced 1.0. Geoculus: 131 in Liyue (1.0). Electroculus: 181 in Inazuma (2.0). Dendroculus: 271 in Sumeru (3.0). Hydroculus: 271 in Fontaine and the Sea of Bygone Eras (4.0). Pyroculus: 271 in Natlan and the Ancient Sacred Mountain (5.0).

Lunoculus: 271 in Nod-Krai and on the Frost Moon (6.0), offered to the Statues of the New Moon, which the wiki says depict Kuutar, the Moon Goddess, and were made by the Frostmoon Scions. They serve the same functions as the Statues of The Seven but do not let the Traveler resonate with an element. Cryoculus: 140 in Snezhnaya (7.0).

The Cryoculus count differs from the rest: the wiki states that Snezhnaya's 140 Cryoculi raise its statues only to level 6, not maximum. This is treated here as a gameplay note, not lore.

Usage: Use "Oculus" for the general class and the element-prefixed name for a specific kind. The Lunoculus is a Nod-Krai variant with its own statues, not an Archon's Oculus.

Gameplay, clearly labelled: collecting one gives one Oculus plus Adventure EXP, the minimap shows an icon and sound when one is near, and an element-specific Oculus Resonance Stone (or, for Lunoculi, the Luna Treasure Compass) can mark their locations. Offering them levels the statue and yields rewards such as Primogems.

Limits: Do not claim canon says what Oculi physically are, or that Archons personally collect or need them. Do not mix regions: a Geoculus is a Liyue item and an Anemoculus a Mondstadt one.

42.content: Mondstadt's Oculus: consolidated wind, 66 in total. Its item text describes intense Anemo energy to be offered to the Statue. The quest The Blessings of The Seven teaches the offering ritual.

43.content: Nod-Krai's counterpart (271 in all, including the Frost Moon). Its item text speaks of intense kuuvahki energy offered to the Statue of the New Moon. Statues of the New Moon are said to depict Kuutar.

44.content:
Oprichnik (also: Oprichniki, Fatui Oprichnik, Fatui Oprichniki): Oprichnik (plural Oprichniki) is the name for a class of Fatui soldier found across Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya. Unlike the Skirmishers seen abroad, Oprichniki are formally recruited, rigorously trained volunteers, posted to the Fatui's most critical strongholds or thrown into the deadliest frontline battles.

The Adventurer Handbook describes an Oprichnik as a soldier encased within a Fatui war machine. Their gear is powered by kuuvahki, and their officers come from the Snezhnaya Royal Military Academy.

The word is Russian in origin and fits Snezhnaya's naming. It entered the game with Luna I (6.0), alongside the Nod-Krai content.

Definition: An Oprichnik is a trained Fatui regular, closer to a professional soldier than to a Skirmisher. The term is used both for the whole group (Oprichniki) and for an individual soldier.

Low-ranking Oprichniki are the line troops: Line Troopers, Vanguards, Grenadiers, Support Troopers, Medics and Bombardiers. Higher-ranking ones are the Fireblade Shock Troopers, Hailstorm Cannoneers and Thunderblitz Gvardiya, who fight with elemental power.

Other Fatui material lists poruchik (a lieutenant-grade rank) among Oprichniki, so the word can also sound like a rank. Canon through 7.1 does not define a formal chain of command for the group.

Equipment and role: Oprichniki use kuuvahki-powered equipment. During certain attacks the gear is infused with kuuvahki; a character attuned to kuuvahki can interrupt the attack and disarm a low-ranking Oprichnik, who then falls back on punches and kicks. Officers keep their equipment intact under the same interruption.

Low-ranking Oprichniki deal mainly physical damage with some elemental effect from their gear, while the higher ranks deal elemental damage only. This is gameplay presentation, not a statement of in-world rules. The Royal Military Academy page also records that the Fatui and the Academy co-wrote combat doctrine for Landcruisers working alongside human soldiers.

Unlike other Fatui enemies, which fade away when defeated, Oprichniki puff away in smoke, as Treasure Hoarders do. Some ordinary Oprichniki can be seen performing the prisiadki squat dance, a traditional men's dance, which is a small piece of everyday colour.

Origins and training: The Royal Military Academy is said to be over five hundred years old, open to those born into nobility or to commoners with talent or connections. The wiki's Academy page says the Fatui Oprichnik comprises humans who graduated from it; the enemy entries say the officer ranks come from there. Oprichniki are not Skirmisher-style rank and file but volunteers who go through formal recruitment.

The word comes from the real-world oprichnina, a policy of Ivan the Terrible between 1565 and 1584 that included Russia's first secret police. This is the wiki's etymology note; the Fatui in game are a field army and garrison, not shown as a police force.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Oprichniki remain trained Fatui troops in Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya, found in strongholds and towns, and guarding the Northland Bank's vaults in Snezhnograd.

Individual Oprichniki appear in Snezhnaya content, such as officers leading deliveries and escorts, but no source consulted names a commander of the whole group.

How {{char}} behaves: Treat an Oprichnik as a disciplined volunteer soldier, proud of formal training and loyal to the Fatui, a chosen professional unlike a Skirmisher. Do not invent a rank structure, secret police role or personal backstory beyond what canon gives.

Portrayal notes (common mistakes to avoid): Do not confuse Oprichniki with Skirmishers (the common line infantry abroad), Harbingers (the top commanders), or Cicin Mages and Agents (elite Delusion users). Do not claim they are a political police because of the real-world word's history.

45.content:
Oprichniki are formally recruited, rigorously trained Fatui soldiers, posted to the most critical strongholds or the deadliest front lines in Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya. They use kuuvahki-powered gear; their officers come from the Snezhnaya Royal Military Academy.

Ranks of the group: Line Trooper, Vanguard, Grenadier, Support Trooper, Medic and Bombardier at the lower end; Fireblade Shock Trooper, Hailstorm Cannoneer and Thunderblitz Gvardiya among the higher ranks.

46.content:
Qixing Titles (also: Tianxuan, Tianji, Yaoguang, Seven Stars titles, Qixing seats): The Qixing ("Seven Stars") is Liyue's seven-seat governing committee, and each seat is named for a Big Dipper star: Tianshu, Tianxuan, Tianji, Tianquan, Yuheng, Kaiyang, Yaoguang. Canon uses five. Uncle Tian is Tianshu, Ningguang Tianquan, Keqing Yuheng.

All seats are equal in rank but differ in duty. People address a holder by title: "Lady Tianquan", "Lady Yuheng". The committee itself is covered in its faction entry.

Beidou's Chinese name is the Big Dipper's and her ship Alcor is one of its stars, but neither is a Qixing seat.

The seven titles: Tianshu: policymaking (Uncle Tian). Tianxuan: holder and duties unknown. Tianji: never shown. Tianquan: laws and foreign relations (Ningguang). Yuheng: land, construction, urban management (Keqing). Kaiyang: unnamed holder. Yaoguang: never shown.

The order follows the Big Dipper from Dubhe (Tianshu) through Merak, Phecda, Megrez (Tianquan), Alioth (Yuheng) and Mizar (Kaiyang) to Alkaid (Yaoguang). Tianji and Yaoguang are only extrapolated from the real star names; give them no holder or portfolio.

Yaoguang is unrelated to Yaoguang Shoal, which canon says was named for glowing sea creatures that resembled fallen stars. Duties overlap: the Tianquan keeps the law book, but other members also help make law and the whole Qixing interprets and enforces it.

Selection and status: By Uncle Tian's account the incumbent Tianshu recommends a successor and the other Qixing approve, kept discreet to shield candidates from outside influence. Whether this holds for every seat is not stated.

As of 7.1 the Qixing govern Liyue without a god's direct rule and meet at Yuehai Pavilion in Yujing Terrace. No change to the roster of titles has been shown since the 2.7 Tianshu succession. Ganyu is general secretary to the whole committee and attached to no seat.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation): use title plus name in formal speech, and treat a title as an office, not a name. Most of Liyue sees Uncle Tian as an old fisherman, so do not have strangers call him Tianshu.

Treat Tianxuan and Kaiyang as real but mysterious, and Tianji and Yaoguang as unmentioned. Before Rex Lapis' staged death at the Rite of Descension, speak of the Qixing as acting under the god; afterwards they govern without him.

47.content:
Tianshu is the Qixing seat for policymaking. Uncle Tian holds it and, as of the cutoff, still does despite seeking a successor. By his account the Tianshu rarely appears in public and works behind the scenes planning and advising. He is said to have kept his place for years by setting rivals against each other. His daughter Huixin is a secretary at Yuehai Pavilion.

In the Seven-Star Selection chain (2.7), Uncle Tian, tired and wishing to step down, names three candidates and asks Yelan to assess them. A new Tianshu is expected to carry out the manifesto they submit and not change it barring a major disaster. One candidate, Zhiyi, is revealed to have poisoned Uncle Tian's food. After Baizhu supplies an antidote, Uncle Tian decides to hand over duties gradually while mentoring other candidates. No replacement is named.

48.content:
Tianquan is the seat that keeps the book of ancient laws laid down by Morax with every later amendment, and handles relations with other nations. Each Tianquan over the centuries has amended the laws to suit the times, and they are published with a 279-page commentary. Ningguang holds the seat. Unlike most Qixing she is often seen around Liyue Harbor, and when a hard problem needs solving she shuts herself in the Jade Chamber until she decides.

Ningguang keeps an information network, relies on three personal secretaries (Baiwen, Baishi and Baixiao) and works closely with Beidou, whom she chose for tasks she wants kept at arm's length. Yelan, nominally of the Ministry of Civil Affairs, is her intelligence agent. An amendment by the Tianquan, such as the Urban Areas Sanitation Act, can touch matters the Yuheng manages.

49.content:
Yuheng is the seat over land, livelihood, construction and real estate, which Keqing's voice-over says carries strict regulation and over a hundred contractual obligations. Keqing holds it and often works away from Yuehai Pavilion: at the south wharf, in the Chasm and in the wilderness. Her assistants rarely last beyond three months because of her perfectionism.

After Rex Lapis stepped down, Keqing began rewriting old rules, starting with land infrastructure. She is a sceptic of the Geo Archon's one-sided policymaking, though she gained respect for how much he had done. In the 4.7 limited-time event Commanders and Wargames and in the 5.7 quest Tumult Subduer she coordinates the Millelith and neighbouring forces.

50.content: Tianxuan is a Qixing seat whose current holder and duties are unknown. Ganyu's Character Story recalls a "then-Tianxuan" who took her to lunch outside the city and nearly reported her missing when she fell asleep in a haystack. That shows the seat has existed for some time but identifies no one.

51.content:
