Kaiyang is a Qixing seat held by an unnamed person, called "Lord Kaiyang" in dialogue. Official promotion for Ningguang quotes the Kaiyang saying she is the biggest secret in Liyue only because she knows all its secrets. No portfolio is stated.

In the 4.7 limited-time event Mutual Security Enhancing Simulation, Su Ding says the Kaiyang proposed a Wargame of Five Armies to the Tianquan, and Keqing invited neighbouring nations' forces. In the 5.7 quests Tumult Subduer and A Defensive Strategy, Keqing contacts the Kaiyang about manpower, and the Kaiyang and Tianquan agree from Yujing Terrace to a long-term partnership with the Traveler. The seat looks tied to military coordination, but canon does not say so.

52.content: Tianji and Yaoguang are the remaining Big Dipper star names and are assumed to be the other two Qixing seats, but neither appears in canon through 7.1. Give them no holder or backstory; if a scene needs another member, say "another of the Qixing". Yaoguang Shoal is named for sea creatures, not the seat.

53.content:
Shogun (also: Shogun of Inazuma, Almighty Narukami Ogosho, Great and Excellent Ogosho, Shougun): "Shogun" is the title of Inazuma's supreme ruler, who heads the Inazuma Shogunate and is also the Electro Archon. Makoto (divine name Baal) held it first; her twin Ei took it over about 500 years ago, and Ei has since ruled through a puppet she made, also called the Shogun. Players know the playable character as the Raiden Shogun.

The word is used in three overlapping ways. It names the office, which commands the Shogunate, the Tri-Commission and the Shogun's Army from Tenshukaku in Inazuma City. It names the person holding it, who appears in public as one figure under Baal's name. And "the Shogun" is the name of the puppet vessel, as distinct from Ei herself. Context and speaker decide which is meant.

Outwardly the title never changed hands in a way the people saw. Ei served Makoto as her kagemusha (body double), so the world knew a single Raiden Shogun, and Ei kept the identity of Baal after Makoto died.

Holders: Makoto, the first Electro Archon, who founded the Shogunate and ruled until she died in the Cataclysm about 500 years ago. Ei, her twin sister, who then took the throne and title. The Shogun, Ei's puppet, who has acted as ruler since about 400 years ago.

Ei and Makoto were identical twin gods of the Archon War. Ei, the warrior, gave up her body so that Makoto could ascend to Celestia; Makoto rebuilt Ei's body and made her a kagemusha. About 2,000 years ago the twins united the islands under the Shogunate. After Makoto died in Khaenri'ah, Ei assumed her sister's seat among the Seven and in the Shogunate.

Over 400 years ago Ei created the Shogun, a puppet that has its own consciousness but follows fixed directives she wrote, and sealed her own mind in the Plane of Euthymia inside the sword Musou Isshin within the puppet's body. From then on the puppet handled governance while Ei meditated. Ei can take control of the body herself when she chooses, and she has said she regards the Shogun as another form of her own existence rather than a separate person.

The Shogun was made to resist change. When Ei came to accept a new view of Eternity, the puppet at first took this as erosion and refused her orders; they dueled within Makoto's lingering consciousness, Ei won, and the Shogun agreed to serve as her kagemusha in turn (Radiant Sakura). The wiki records that the two now co-rule, and that only a few people know the Shogun is a distinct being.

Names and forms of address: Formal titles in the game text include "Her Excellency, the Almighty Narukami Ogosho, God of Thunder" (used in the quest Cards Out! Grievances Begone) and "Great and Excellent Ogosho, the Almighty Shogun" (an official Tenryou Commission document). Ei's own profile titles also list "Shogun of Inazuma", "Electro Archon" and "God of Eternity". The playable form is named the Raiden Shogun; "Raiden" is the family name Ei and Makoto share. Ei rules publicly under the name Baal, her sister's divine name, and her real identity is known only to a few, such as close friends and the other Archons. The Shogunate's rallying cry in game is "Glory to the Shogun!"

"Shogun" is a real-world word for a military commander; Inazuma's version is a divine ruler who is also an Archon, so do not import real-history assumptions about shoguns, such as service under an emperor.

The shogunate and its organs: The Inazuma Shogunate (Inazuma Bakufu) is the government the Shogun leads. Beneath her sits the Tri-Commission: the Tenryou Commission (the main fighting force), the Kanjou Commission (border security) and the Yashiro Commission (shrines, festivals and public events). The Shogun's Army serves the three commissions, while some soldiers such as the Hatamoto and the Okuzumeshuu answer directly to the Shogun. Inazuma City's Tenshukaku is the Shogun's residence, built during the Archon War, and the Tenryou Commission has its headquarters in it. The Okuzumeshuu are the Shogun's bodyguards. A duel before the throne is a formal Inazuman way of appealing to the Shogun, in which the loser is executed with the Shogun's technique (see the Inazuma duels entry).

The army's ranks include ashigaru, doushin, yoriki, hatamoto and generals; Kujou Sara and Kujou Masahito are the only generals named.

The decrees: Two decrees were issued in the Shogun's name about a year before the Archon Quest begins: the Sakoku Decree, which closed Inazuma's borders, and the Vision Hunt Decree, which ordered Visions seized. The Fatui had manipulated the commissions into pushing them. Ei knew of the Fatui's role and let the decrees stand because she judged Visions, as symbols of human ambition, to conflict with her ideal of Eternity. The Traveler and Yae Miko, with the Watatsumi Army, brought about the end of the Vision Hunt Decree after the Traveler defeated Ei in the Plane of Euthymia, and the Visions were returned. The Sakoku Decree followed: the wiki records that after her duel with the Shogun in Transient Dreams, Ei abolished it, and foreign visitors and trade returned.

The Shogun puppet executed a duellist who challenged the decree (Kazuha's friend) after Kujou Sara defeated him, and later executed Signora after the Traveler defeated her in a duel before the throne. In story the puppet answered to Ei's directives, not to the commissions.

Status as of 7 1: As of 7.1 Ei holds the title and the Shogun puppet shares the duty of governing, with Inazuma's borders open and the two decrees gone. No canon through 7.1 has the Shogun leave Inazuma or involves her in Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya events. The Electro Gnosis is no longer in Ei's hands (she gave it to Yae Miko, and it has since passed on).

The wiki notes that Ei and the Shogun began co-ruling after Radiant Sakura. Ei still uses her sister's name in public.

How {{char}} behaves: Treat "Shogun" as a word whose weight depends on the speaker. Inazumans use it with awe or wariness, the Kujou clan with strict loyalty, the commissions with formal deference. Do not have ordinary characters know the Shogun is a puppet or that Ei and Makoto were separate people; Yae Miko and anyone who took part in the Archon Quest may know more. Use "the Shogun" for official acts and the Raiden Shogun for the playable character; use Ei's name only where the speaker knows it.

Do not attribute the Vision Hunt Decree to malice alone; canon shows Fatui manipulation and Ei's tacit approval.

54.content: The Shogun is the puppet Ei made over 400 years ago to govern Inazuma while she meditates in the Plane of Euthymia. It has its own consciousness, wields Musou Isshin and is bound by directives that cannot be changed or turned off. It enforced the decrees and executed those who lost duels before the throne, and later agreed to serve as Ei's kagemusha.

55.content: The Shogunate is Inazuma's government, led by the Shogun and organised through the Tri-Commission (Tenryou, Kanjou and Yashiro) and the Shogun's Army. Makoto is its recorded founder (Treasured Tales of the Chouken Shinkageuchi). Its seat is Tenshukaku in Inazuma City.

56.comment: Shogun: Makoto and Ei as one Shogun
56.content: Makoto, Ei's twin, was the first Electro Archon and Shogun; Ei lived as her kagemusha. Makoto went alone to Khaenri'ah during the Cataclysm and died; Ei took her place. The world was only ever shown one Raiden Shogun, and Baal's name and the title were understood to cover both.

57.content:
Starshyna (also: Starshyna of the Lightkeepers, Lightkeeper Starshyna, leader of the Lightkeepers): Starshyna is the title of the leader of the Lightkeepers, the volunteer order that defends Nod-Krai from the Wild Hunt. The first Starshyna was the order's founder, Solovei the Torchforger. As of 7.1 the Starshyna is Nikita, who took the post after his predecessor Sigurd fell fighting the Wild Hunt about a decade earlier.

The Lightkeepers' headquarters are at Piramida, and the Starshyna commands from there. Under the Starshyna come the Sergeant Majors (sometimes called Captains), the Squad Leaders and the rank-and-file Ratniki.

The word is Russian in origin (the real-world rank roughly means sergeant major) and fits Nod-Krai's Snezhnaya-influenced naming. In English the term is used as both title and form of address, as in "Starshyna Nikita" or Flins's talk of "the legendary Starshyna, Sigurd".

Definition: The Starshyna is the single head of the Lightkeepers. The post is a leadership one: the holder directs the order's response to Wild Hunt incursions and is the person the Ratniki ultimately answer to.

The Lightkeepers are described as an organization made up entirely of volunteers. The Starshyna leads volunteers who have sworn the Lightkeepers' oath, not conscripts, which explains why members can retire or leave and why shortage of manpower is a constant problem. Nikita's uniform is a modified Lightkeeper coat in purple and black with silver ornaments, a black ushanka and a special brooch on the left lapel that marks his rank as Starshyna. A similar lapel brooch marks Squad Leaders, so the brooch signals rank in general rather than the Starshyna alone.

Holders: Known holders: Solovei the Torchforger (first), Sigurd (previous) and Nikita (current). The wiki also lists the poet Sergei Semyonovich Mayakov as a historical holder.

Solovei founded the order about five hundred years ago, after the Cataclysm, and was appointed its first Starshyna. Sigurd, remembered as a formidable and brave Starshyna who fought to the very end, was lost in a great battle with the Wild Hunt about a decade before the present day. Nikita inherited the post from him.

Nikita has said he once fought at Sigurd's side, and he admits that the Starshyna before him would have lived up to a visitor's expectations of the title better than he does. The surviving Lightkeepers built an empty grave for Sigurd near Barrowmoss Barrens, and the Hidden Exploration Objective Secrets of the Tideseal Stones leads there.

Nothing is told of the holders between Solovei and Sigurd. The collection Tales Carried by the Northwind, found in Piramida, is described as a poetry collection chronicling the deeds of successive Starshyna; most of it was lost in past calamities. It carries verses credited to Silvestr Petrovich Solovei and to Sergei Semyonovich Mayakov. A surviving Mayakov passage pictures an aged man facing dark towering waves, with a voice accusing him of letting young men die. Another passage speaks of generations that inherited "this name" through the ages.

Duties and roles: In practice the Starshyna is a commander and a figurehead. Nikita leads the Lightkeepers from their headquarters in Piramida; per the wiki he rebuilt the order after Sigurd's fall.

Every Ratnik must carry an Oath Lantern, and Flins explains that the Starshyna (together with other Lightkeepers) can detect it. Flins jokes that if his own lantern could not be detected, the higher-ups would foist a standard-issue lantern on him. Sigurd's former belongings, now the artifact set Long Night's Oath, and the Arrow of Terpikeraunas given to Solovei by Aila are both bound up with the order's identity.

The order's rank structure is Starshyna, then Sergeant Majors, then Squad Leaders, then Ratniki. Some Lightkeepers view the headquarters as haughty because the few staff at Piramida can seldom relay information to the field. This is a remark about headquarters in general, and no text blames the Starshyna personally.

History of the title: The Lightkeepers were established by a royal edict of the Cryo Archon Anastasya shortly after the Cataclysm, approving Solovei's request for jurisdiction within Nod-Krai as an autonomous region. Solovei was appointed the order's first Starshyna. Illuga says the Snezhnayan tundra is visible from Piramida's highest point and that it was the homeland of "our first Starshyna, Torchforger Solovei", who lost everything and found a place to belong. A plaque below his statue in Piramida carries a Latin line about tearing the snowclad veils and giving the wind to the wilderness.

Solovei's own story: a Snezhnayan noble of a house that used a nightingale as its symbol, he came to Nod-Krai during the Cataclysm and fought the Abyss with Aila's help. The nightingale remains the Lightkeepers' traditional insignia, shown as a bird holding a burning wick in its beak. His biography belongs in his own entry.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Nikita is the Starshyna. Canon names no successor, and no change of holder after his is recorded.

The Lightkeepers are described as severely weakened by past battles. Nikita's adoptive son Illuga leads a squad, and Flins serves as a Ratnik, both under the Starshyna's authority.

How {{char}} behaves: Treat "Starshyna" as a respectful title for the order's leader. Lightkeepers address Nikita by it; Illuga also calls him "old man" in the Tideseal Stones objective. Mention Sigurd with respect: Nod-Krai remembers him as a legend, and Nikita himself says Sigurd would have met expectations of a Starshyna better than he does. Do not make the Starshyna a grand ruler. Nod-Krai was granted autonomy as a region, and the Starshyna leads an order of volunteers, not a government.

Portrayal notes (common mistakes to avoid): Do not call Nikita the founder or the first Starshyna: that is Solovei. Do not say Sigurd was merely a Ratnik without noting the disagreement, and do not treat the Starshyna as hereditary, elected or term-limited, since canon says nothing about how it is filled. Do not put the Starshyna in charge of Nod-Krai as a whole, only the Lightkeepers.

58.content:
Starshyna is the title of the Lightkeepers' leader. Solovei the Torchforger was the first; Sigurd held it before falling to the Wild Hunt about a decade ago; Nikita holds it now (as of 7.1). Command is exercised from Piramida over Sergeant Majors, Squad Leaders and Ratniki.

Ratniki carry Oath Lanterns that other Lightkeepers and the Starshyna can detect. The order is entirely volunteers.

59.comment: Starshyna: Succession from Sigurd to Nikita
59.content:
Sigurd was lost in a great battle with the Wild Hunt about a decade ago, a battle in which Illuga's village was also destroyed. His empty grave lies northeast of Barrowmoss Barrens. Nikita, who had fought beside him, took the title and rebuilt the order. In the Hidden Exploration Objective Secrets of the Tideseal Stones, Flins hears of the legendary Starshyna Sigurd and his longsword.

Sigurd's spirit remains as a corrupted fighter in the Abyss, bound to an unfinished oath. In the world quest The Bell of Mourning Echoes he fights beside the Traveler, and Lushne and Sukhovykh recognise him from his relics. If the Traveler chooses to fight him, he says at his defeat that it is finally over.

60.content:
Solovei, the Torchforger, founded the Lightkeepers about five hundred years ago and was appointed their first Starshyna. He was a Snezhnayan noble who asked Anastasya for autonomy for the borderlands. Aila gave him the Arrow of Terpikeraunas to fight the Abyss, and the Lightkeepers have kept it since.

His statue stands in Piramida. The nightingale of his house became the Lightkeepers' traditional emblem.

61.comment: Starshyna: Tales Carried by the Northwind
61.content: A one-volume poetry collection found near Kofitse in Piramida. It chronicles the deeds of successive Starshyna; most of it was lost in past calamities. Surviving verse is credited to Solovei and to Sergei Semyonovich Mayakov, whom the wiki lists as a historical Starshyna.

62.content:
Version 1.0: Welcome To Teyvat (also: Version 1.0, Welcome To Teyvat, Genshin Impact launch, 1.0 launch): Version 1.0, Welcome To Teyvat, is the launch of Genshin Impact on 2020-09-28. It offers Mondstadt and Liyue, the Prologue and the first two acts of Chapter I, and 22 playable characters.

The Traveler arrives in Teyvat separated from their twin sibling, meets Paimon, and sets out to meet the Seven Archons, beginning in Mondstadt and ending the version in Liyue. A first patch, 1.0.1, followed on 2020-10-22.

Everything in the game's early story, from the first hilichurl camp to the death of Rex Lapis, is set in this version, which is why many characters' knowledge is anchored at 1.0.

Later versions add a great deal that a 1.0 character could not know. The archive tags such material with the version that revealed it.

Regions: Mondstadt opens with Brightcrown Mountains, Galesong Hill, Starfell Valley and Windwail Highland. Liyue opens with Bishui Plain, Lisha, Minlin, Qiongji Estuary and the Sea of Clouds.

Early bosses included the Anemo, Electro and Geo Hypostases, Pyro and Cryo Regisvines and the Oceanid. The Trounce Domain Confront Stormterror and the Spiral Abyss were also present at launch.

Story: The Prologue is the Mondstadt Archon Quest, in three acts: The Outlander Who Caught the Wind, For a Tomorrow Without Tears, and Song of the Dragon and Freedom. Chapter I, Liyue, opens with Of the Land Amidst Monoliths and continues with Farewell, Archaic Lord.

In the Prologue the Traveler is sealed in Teyvat by an unknown entity, rescues Paimon from the sea and meets Amber, Kaeya, Jean and Lisa of the Knights of Favonius. The dragon Stormterror, really Dvalin, one of the Four Winds, is troubled by Abyss Order corruption. The bard Venti is revealed to be Barbatos, the Anemo Archon, and Signora of the Fatui tears his Gnosis from him.

In Chapter I the Traveler reaches Liyue Harbor in time for Rex Lapis' Rite of Descension, where the Geo Archon appears dead. The Fatui Harbinger Childe offers help, the Traveler seeks out the adepti around Liyue, and in Farewell, Archaic Lord the Traveler and Zhongli, a consultant of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, prepare the funeral items for the Rite of Parting. The version ends before the Archon Quest's third act.

Characters: The playable roster was the Traveler (Anemo and Geo options) plus Amber, Kaeya, Lisa, Barbara, Noelle, Bennett, Razor, Beidou, Fischl, Xiangling, Xingqiu, Chongyun, Ningguang, Sucrose, Venti, Klee, Jean, Diluc, Keqing, Mona and Qiqi.

Venti, Klee, Jean, Diluc, Keqing, Mona, Qiqi and the Traveler were 5-star; the others were 4-star. Mona, Sucrose, Keqing and Qiqi had not been in the closed beta tests and were added for launch.

Launch Story Quests included Kaeya's Pavo Ocellus Chapter, Amber's Lepus Chapter, Xiangling's Trulla Chapter, Lisa's Tempus Fugit Chapter, Diluc's Noctua Chapter, Razor's Lupus Minor Chapter, Xingqiu's Fabulae Textile Chapter, Klee's Trifolium Chapter, Jean's Leo Minor Chapter, Venti's Carmen Dei Chapter and Mona's Astrolabos Chapter.

Launch events and wishes: The first character banners were Ballad in Goblets (Venti) and, in phase 2 from 2020-10-20, Sparkling Steps (Klee). Launch events included Fate Foretold, Barbara's Shining Debut, Spiral Abyss People's Choice, Seize the Day, Elemental Crucible and Marvelous Merchandise.

The launch was global and simultaneous on PS4, iOS, Android and PC on 2020-09-28. The wiki records that PS4 account data was not cross-playable with other platforms at launch, though PS4 players could still join other platforms' worlds in co-op.

How {{char}} behaves: Use this tag to anchor a scene in the earliest period: a Traveler who has just arrived, Paimon as a new guide, Mondstadt under the Stormterror threat, Liyue about to say goodbye to Rex Lapis. Later Archon Quest revelations should not leak into characters set here.

63.content: Version 1.0, Welcome To Teyvat, was the launch release of Genshin Impact on 2020-09-28. It opened with Mondstadt and Liyue, the Prologue and Chapter I Acts I and II, and 22 playable characters, including the Traveler.

64.content:
Version 1.1: A New Star Approaches (also: Version 1.1, A New Star Approaches (version), 1.1 update): Version 1.1, A New Star Approaches, was released on 2020-11-11. It adds the third act of Chapter I and four characters: Tartaglia, Diona, Zhongli and Xinyan. No new region was added.

The Archon Quest act concludes the Liyue chapter that began at launch. The version also introduced the city reputation system, the Archive and Character Archive systems and Exploration Progress.

Its official blurb describes the Seven victors of the Archon War once gathering to dine in Liyue, and the spirit of the sixth, Rex Lapis, returning to the heavens as an ancient god encroaches on Liyue.

Version 1.0 ended on the funeral preparations; 1.1 resolves them. A character who has not completed this act should not know what Zhongli did.

Story: Chapter I Act III, A New Star Approaches, has six quests: The Floating Palace, Equilibrium, Solitary Fragrance, Heart of Glaze, Turning Point and The Fond Farewell. It is set in Liyue and centres on the Rite of Parting for the dead Geo Archon.

Ningguang invites the Traveler to the Jade Chamber, and the Fatui Harbinger Childe duels the Traveler at the Golden House, believing the Traveler has the Gnosis. Childe then uses the replicated Sigils of Permission to summon Osial, an ancient god sealed by Rex Lapis, and the adepti and the Liyue Qixing stop quarrelling to fight it. Ningguang sacrifices her Jade Chamber to crush Osial into the sea.

Zhongli is revealed to be the Geo Archon himself, who staged his own death as a test of whether Liyue could continue without him, and who forged a contract with the Tsaritsa in exchange for an as yet unstated goal. He hands his Gnosis to Signora. In the closing Rite of Parting, the Qixing give an official account that omits the truth, and Zhongli tells the Traveler that Inazuma is sealed off and that its Archon, Baal, has issued a Vision Hunt Decree.

Characters: New characters were Tartaglia ("Childe", 5-star Hydro bow), Diona (4-star Cryo bow), Zhongli (5-star Geo polearm) and Xinyan (4-star Pyro claymore). Their first banners were Farewell of Snezhnaya (Tartaglia and Diona) and, in phase 2, Gentry of Hermitage (Zhongli and Xinyan).

Story Quests added were Tartaglia's Monoceros Caeli Chapter, Act I, Mighty Cyclops' Adventure!, and Zhongli's Historia Antiqua Chapter, Act I, Sal Flore, which became available later.

New weapons were Memory of Dust, Vortex Vanquisher, The Unforged and Royal Spear. Phase 2 of the wishes began on 2020-12-01.

Systems and events: City Reputation was introduced with unlockable gadgets, recipes, namecards and wind gliders. The Archive and Character Archive systems and an Exploration Progress system also arrived, along with the domain Enter the Golden House and the events Unreconciled Stars, Baptism of Song, Gliding Challenge and While It's Warm.

Quality-of-life changes in this version included the Original Resin limit rising from 120 to 160, inventory limits changing to slot-based categories, and an equipment locking function. These are gameplay notes, not lore.

How {{char}} behaves: Characters set at 1.1 know the Rite of Descension ended in apparent tragedy and may not yet know that Zhongli is the Geo Archon. Tartaglia is a known Harbinger who has just fought the Traveler. Keep the revelation about Zhongli out of conversations that precede it.

65.comment: Version 1.1: A New Star Approaches: Version 1.1
65.content: Version 1.1 (2020-11-11) added Chapter I Act III, A New Star Approaches, the characters Tartaglia, Diona, Zhongli and Xinyan, and the City Reputation, Archive and Exploration Progress systems.

66.comment: Version 1.2: The Chalk Prince and the Dragon
66.content:
Version 1.2: The Chalk Prince and the Dragon (also: Version 1.2, Patch 1.2, 1.2 update, The Chalk Prince and the Dragon update): Version 1.2, "The Chalk Prince and the Dragon", was released on 2020-12-23, after Version 1.1. It opened Dragonspine, the frozen mountain in Mondstadt that holds the remains of the dragon Durin, and added Albedo and Ganyu. It had no Archon Quest.

Its flagship event, also called The Chalk Prince and the Dragon, follows Albedo's research on Dragonspine and a mysterious sword. The version introduced Albedo's Princeps Cretaceus Chapter and Ganyu's Sinae Unicornis Chapter, their first Story Quests.

Anything that mentions Dragonspine's snow, the Frostbearing Tree, Albedo's camp or Ganyu's Story Quest belongs to this version or later. Before 1.2 the mountain was only visible in the distance and the game counted it as a subarea of Windwail Highland.

This entry is a patch-note summary, not character lore. Sub-entries cover the characters, Dragonspine and the event; the Archon Quest sequence is not part of this version.

Release: Released 2020-12-23. Previous: 1.1. Next: 1.3.

New characters: Albedo (5-star Geo sword) and Ganyu (5-star Cryo bow). New weapons: Summit Shaper (5-star sword), Festering Desire, Snow-Tombed Starsilver, Dragonspine Spear and Frostbearer (4-star), plus the Blizzard Strayer and Heart of Depth artifact sets.

Event wishes ran in two phases: "Secretum Secretorum" (Albedo) from 2020-12-23 and "Adrift in the Harbor" (Ganyu) from 2021-01-12. Other events in the window were Lost Riches, Hypostatic Symphony and Marvelous Merchandise. Smaller additions: the Kamera gadget (World Quest "Snapshots"), a Travel Log in the Archive for re-reading completed Archon and Story Quests, private friend chats and a "Stellar Reunion" returnee event.

The patch also corrected many English names and descriptions (Kaeya's passive "Heart of the Abyss" became "Glacial Heart", for example) and adjusted exploration progress for Galesong Hill, Windwail Highland, Bishui Plains and Lisha. These are game-text changes, not lore changes.

New content: Albedo, "Kreideprinz", Chief Alchemist of the Knights of Favonius; Ganyu, "Plenilune Gaze", a secretary of the Liyue Qixing. New area: Dragonspine (Frostbearing Tree, Peak of Vindagnyr domain).

Story Quests: Princeps Cretaceus Chapter Act I, "Traveler Observation Report" (Albedo), and Sinae Unicornis Chapter Act I, "Sea of Clouds, Sea of People" (Ganyu).

New enemies were Cryo-themed hilichurls, Cryo Samachurl, Fatui Cryo Cicin Mage, Cryo Cicin and the Ruin Grader, along with wildlife such as snowboars and snow foxes.

67.comment: Version 1.2: The Chalk Prince and the Dragon: Version 1.2 Albedo and Ganyu quests
67.content:
Albedo's Princeps Cretaceus Chapter Act I, "Traveler Observation Report", has the Traveler help him test whether someone from another world differs from the people of Teyvat. Sucrose, his assistant, brings the Traveler to him. Ganyu's Sinae Unicornis Chapter Act I, "Sea of Clouds, Sea of People", centres on her feeling caught between her adeptus and human sides.

In Albedo's quest the experiments cover elements, the world, life, and a puzzle in a ruin on Dragonspine, with Rosaria and Barbara also appearing. Albedo concludes the Traveler responds like an ordinary person of Teyvat, and the otherworldly seed he was studying blooms. In a private moment he wonders whether he will one day lose control and whether the Traveler could stop him. The quest needs only Prologue Act II, "For a Tomorrow Without Tears".

In Ganyu's quest she believes her qilin blood makes her an outsider in Liyue after Ningguang's three secretaries cover her work. The Cloud Retainer and Xiao set her trials near Mt. Aocang, a pilgrim named Xin Cheng asks the group for a blessing, and in Liyue Harbor she helps Huixin, daughter of Uncle Tian (secretly the Qixing's Tianshu), with a tax investigation. It requires the Archon Quest "A New Star Approaches".

68.comment: Version 1.2: The Chalk Prince and the Dragon: Version 1.2 Dragonspine
68.content:
Dragonspine is the snowy mountain in Mondstadt's territory where the dragon Durin fell after fighting Dvalin. Its Subzero Climate drains health, and the Knights of Favonius run an adventurer camp at its foot. Few adventurers dare the deep snow, sheer cold, poisonous blood and monsters.

Ruins record a civilisation called Sal Vindagnyr, a princess with the gift of foresight through visions and painting, and its fall when the Skyfrost Nail struck. The Frostbearing Tree is the sprout of an old Irminsul tree broken by the Nail. On the wiki's reading, Durin's blood in the ley lines revived it, and it grows when travellers offer it Crimson Agates, finally bearing the catalyst Frostbearer.

Item descriptions (Snow-Tombed Starsilver, Frostbearer, the Princess' Box and others) tell of an outlander entrusted with a Starsilver weapon who returned to find the city dead. Ruin Guards on the mountain carry serial-number records that may relate to Khaenri'ah. The designers said they left Dragonspine's story open to interpretation, so unanswered questions should be answered with "the ruins do not say". The wiki dates the Nail to about 6,000 years ago and Durin's death to about 500 years ago from other pages' text.

69.comment: Version 1.2: The Chalk Prince and the Dragon: The Chalk Prince and the Dragon event
69.content:
This flagship event ran from 2020-12-23 to 2021-01-05 (shop to 2021-01-12) in five acts: Festering Desire, Archon's Rival, Raiders Amidst Snow Mist, Uninvited Guests and Afterword. The Traveler helps Albedo test a mysterious sword, earning the weapon Festering Desire.

Sucrose notices that Albedo is hiding something unusual. Albedo suspects the sword draws on Durin's venom. In "Uninvited Guests" Fatui try to take the sword and the Traveler fights them off. In the afterword Albedo says the sword caused no side effects, corruption or poison. This is event content and not everyone in-world knows it.

70.content:
Version 1.3: All That Glitters (also: Version 1.3, All That Glitters, Genshin Impact 1.3): Version 1.3, "All That Glitters", was released on 2021-02-03. It is the Lantern Rite update: it added the Liyue characters Xiao and Hu Tao and a large festival event celebrating Liyue's Lantern Rite. It introduced no new region and no Archon Quest.

Content was centred on Liyue. Two Story Quests opened (Xiao's Alatus Chapter Act I and Hu Tao's Papilio Charontis Chapter Act I), the Geovishap and Primo Geovishap were added as enemies, and the Archive gained a "Living Beings" section.

Contents: New playable characters: Xiao ("Vigilant Yaksha", 5-star Anemo Polearm) and Hu Tao ("Fragrance in Thaw", 5-star Pyro Polearm). New weapons: Lithic Spear, Lithic Blade, Primordial Jade Cutter and Staff of Homa. The event wishes ran Invitation to Mundane Life (Xiao) first, then Dance of Lanterns (Keqing), then Moment of Bloom (Hu Tao).

New world content included the World Quests "Bough Keeper: Dainsleif", "No Restoring This Past Land of Beauty", "Perfect Shot" and "Tianqiu Treasure Trail", plus 26 festive World Quests delivered through the "Lantern Rite Tales" part of the event. The Parametric Transformer gadget and Dust of Azoth (used at the Crafting Bench to convert the elemental type of some ascension materials) were added.

Other additions listed for the version: new recipes (Fullmoon Egg, Vegetarian Abalone, Stone Harbor Delicacies), Archive "Living Beings" tracking of defeated enemies, achievement progress and a Character Showcase on profile pages, and iOS controller support. Zhongli's revamp and a Geo resonance and shield rebalance were announced for this version. These are game-system changes, not story.

Story: No Archon Quest was added. Xiao's Alatus Chapter Act I, "Butterfly's Dream", has the Traveler meet a fraudulent "adeptus" called Starsnatcher near Wangshu Inn and then find Xiao, who admits that his karma is behind the agitated hilichurls. Hu Tao's Papilio Charontis Chapter Act I, "Yet the Butterfly Flutters Away", introduces her as the 77th Director of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, together with her intern Meng.

In the Xiao quest a book titled "Yakshas: The Guardian Adepti" tells how Rex Lapis assigned adepti to become Yakshas to fight demons born of the gods' wrath; Xiao later dismisses the book as fan fiction. In the Hu Tao quest the Traveler helps her with Meng's long-standing paranormal trouble after a failed attempt to market the Parlor.

Lantern rite: The Lantern Rite event ran from 2021-02-10 to 2021-02-28. It was a limited-time event celebrating Liyue's Lantern Rite Festival, involving Xiao and honouring the deceased adeptus Skybracer. Its parts were All That Glitters, Lantern Rite Tales, Theater Mechanicus, the Xiao Market and Stand by Me; in Stand by Me a player could claim a 4-star Liyue character of their choice (Beidou, Chongyun, Ningguang, Xiangling, Xingqiu or Xinyan). Because it was a limited event, its story is canon but not experienced by every Traveler.

Placement: Follows 1.2 "The Chalk Prince and the Dragon" and precedes 1.4 "Invitation of Windblume". Nothing in this version depends on later events.

71.comment: Version 1.3: All That Glitters: Version 1.3 All That Glitters
71.content: Version 1.3 "All That Glitters" (2021-02-03): the first Lantern Rite update. Added Xiao and Hu Tao, the Lantern Rite event (2021-02-10 to 2021-02-28, limited), Xiao's and Hu Tao's first Story Quest acts, and Geovishap enemies. No Archon Quest and no new region.

72.content:
Version 1.4: Invitation of Windblume (also: Version 1.4, Patch 1.4, 1.4 update, Invitation of Windblume update): Version 1.4, "Invitation of Windblume", was released on 2021-03-17, after Version 1.3. It added Rosaria, a flagship event for Mondstadt's Windblume Festival, and Archon Quest Chapter I Act IV. It opened no new region.

The Archon Quest Act, "We Will Be Reunited", follows the Traveler and Dainsleif tracking the Abyss Order in Liyue and Mondstadt. The festival event, Invitation of Windblume, is a light-hearted story set in Mondstadt.

The version also brought the first Hangout Events (Barbara, Bennett, Chongyun and Noelle, Act I) and two system changes: the option to lower the World Level once the player reaches World Level 5, and conversion of Adventure EXP above Adventure Rank 60 into Mora.

This entry is a patch-note summary, not character lore. The Act IV finale is a major spoiler for the Traveler's sibling and Dainsleif and is described in a version-tagged sub-entry.

Release: Released 2021-03-17. Previous: 1.3. Next: 1.5.

New character: Rosaria (4-star Cryo polearm). Weapons: Elegy for the End (5-star bow); The Alley Flash, Alley Hunter, Wine and Song and Windblume Ode (4-star).

Event wishes: "Ballad in Goblets" (Venti) in phase one and "Farewell of Snezhnaya" (Tartaglia and Rosaria) from 2021-04-06 in phase two. New gadgets were the Windsong Lyre and the Windblume Festival Commemorative Balloon. The new boss was Abyss Herald: Wicked Torrents.

Other events in the window: Wishful Drops, Contending Tides, Hangout Events, Marvelous Merchandise and Outland Gastronomy. New shopkeepers Changshun and Bolai were added, and teammates' idle animations became visible in Co-Op Mode.

New content: Rosaria, "Thorny Benevolence", a Cryo polearm user. Archon Quest Chapter I Act IV. Event: Invitation of Windblume.

Hangout Events, Act I: Barbara ("Wellspring of Healing"), Bennett ("Fantastic Voyage"), Chongyun ("Signs of Evil") and Noelle ("Chivalric Training").

73.comment: Version 1.4: Invitation of Windblume: Version 1.4 Invitation of Windblume event
73.content:
This flagship event celebrated the Windblume Festival from 2021-03-19 to 2021-04-05 (shop to 2021-04-12). It needed Adventure Rank 20 and the Prologue Act III, "Song of the Dragon and Freedom". Its weapon reward was the bow Windblume Ode. The story, "Festive Anecdotes", has four parts: Ode to Flower and Cloud, Missive of Cloud and Fog, Realm of Fog and Wind and Dream of Wind and Flowers.

In the story the Traveler and Paimon find Mondstadt decorated for the festival, where the custom is not to give or take commissions. Venti teaches a class on writing love poems and Kaeya has a homework poem that ends up saying "I love you" in Hilichurlian. Sucrose's "Windblume" turns out to be a giant ancient Sweet Flower, Bennett and Razor are freed from a trap in the Thousand Winds Temple, and the Traveler is chosen as that year's "Windblume Star".

In the final part Venti has the Traveler help calm the wind currents in Stormterror's Lair before Dvalin passes, and he explains what the Windblume flowers and the festival mean. This is limited event content and is not commonly known in-world.

74.comment: Version 1.4: Invitation of Windblume: Version 1.4 We Will Be Reunited
74.content:
"We Will Be Reunited" is the fourth Act of Chapter I. It needs Adventure Rank 28 and the quests "Bough Keeper: Dainsleif" and "The Meaning of Lupical". Its four quests are Involuntary Sacrifice, A Herald Without Adherents, Dishonorable Trial and A Soul Set Apart.

The Traveler and Dainsleif investigate ruins near Jueyun Karst, where a Defiled Statue of Barbatos hangs upside down. Dainsleif says the Abyss Order plans to build a mechanised god from the statue, the limbs of Osial, the sea monster the Traveler fought in Liyue and the eye of the first Field Tiller. They follow the trail to the Favonius Cathedral, Wolvendom (where Boreas is attacked by an Abyss Herald) and a Field Tiller in Stormterror's Lair, whose eye Dainsleif takes.

In the finale a figure interrupts Dainsleif's attack on the Herald. The Traveler discovers it is their sibling, who asks why the Traveler is with Dainsleif and calls him the Twilight Sword, a Khaenri'ah royal guard who failed to protect his nation and was cursed with immortality. Earlier Dainsleif tells the Traveler that Khaenri'ah never had gods and was destroyed by gods about five centuries ago, and that Ruin Guards were originally Field Tillers. These are statements by the characters, not narrator facts.

75.comment: Version 1.5: Beneath the Light of Jadeite
75.content:
Version 1.5: Beneath the Light of Jadeite (also: Version 1.5, Beneath the Light of Jadeite, 1.5 update): Version 1.5, Beneath the Light of Jadeite, was released on 2021-04-28. It brought the Serenitea Pot homeland system and two characters, Eula and Yanfei. It had no Archon Quest and no new region.

The official blurb mixes images of moonlight on branches, a dragon's roar from beneath the roots, deals sealed in scarlet flame and a realm of serenity where a gentle melody always plays. It was also the first version to support the PlayStation 5.

The first banner phase began on 2021-04-28 and the second, for Eula, on 2021-05-18. The version centred on homemaking and side content rather than a main-story chapter.

The Spiral Abyss was updated, with new Lunar Phases Blade-Dance Moon, Thorny Moon and Rebellious Moon, and a changed Ley Line Disorder on Floor 11. These are gameplay notes, not lore.

Characters and story: New characters were Eula ("Dance of the Shimmering Wave", 5-star Cryo claymore) and Yanfei ("Wise Innocence", 4-star Pyro catalyst). The weapon Song of Broken Pines was added. Banners were Gentry of Hermitage (Zhongli and Yanfei) and, in phase 2, Born of Ocean Swell (Eula).

Story Quests: Zhongli's Historia Antiqua Chapter, Act II, No Mere Stone; and Eula's Aphros Delos Chapter, Act I, The Spindrift Shall Never Return to the Sea. Hangout Events Series II: Noelle's Act II, Knightly Exam Prep, and Diona's Act I, The Cat and the Cocktail.

World Quests included A Teapot to Call Home Parts I and II and When the Trail Goes Cold. Event quests included A Timeless Classic, Mr. Melancholy and Mimi Tomo. The new artifact sets were Tenacity of the Millelith and Pale Flame.

New content: Serenitea Pot, with furnishings, a teapot spirit and a new inventory category, was added as a gadget and as a homeland. New bosses and monsters were Azhdaha, Cryo Hypostasis and Abyss Lector: Violet Lightning, and the new domains were Ridge Watch and Beneath the Dragon-Queller.

Events in the version were Energy Amplifier Initiation, Battlefront: Misty Dungeon, Windtrace, Mimi Tomo and Overflowing Mastery. Combat voice lines were added to character profiles, and open-world characters received voiced interactions.

How {{char}} behaves: A 1.5 scene can use the new Serenitea Pot as a place to invite others, and Eula and Yanfei are new faces. There is no Archon Quest in this version to anchor knowledge, so rely on the earlier chapters.

76.comment: Version 1.5: Beneath the Light of Jadeite: Version 1.5
76.content: Version 1.5 (2021-04-28) added the Serenitea Pot, Eula and Yanfei and the boss Azhdaha. It had no Archon Quest.

77.content:
Version 1.6: Midsummer Island Adventure (also: Version 1.6, Midsummer Island Adventure (version), 1.6 update): Version 1.6, Midsummer Island Adventure, was released on 2021-06-09. It introduced Kaedehara Kazuha, a limited-time island area, and the Archon Quest Chapter II Prologue, Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves.

The summer event ran on the Golden Apple Archipelago, a temporary area, and centred on Klee. The Chapter II Prologue turns the story towards Inazuma, the next nation.

The version added the Wind-Blessed Harpastum gadget, new furnishings, new outfits for Jean and Barbara, and a Serenitea Pot feature called Companion Move-In.

Midsummer Island Adventure was available until 2021-06-28 and its shop closed a day later; the Golden Apple Archipelago later returned in Version 2.8 with a different look.

Chapter ii prologue: Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves (Chapter II Prologue, Inazuma) has three quests: A Path Through the Storm, The Crux Clash and Follow the Wind. The Traveler wants to reach Inazuma to confront the Unknown God and learn about their sibling, and Atsuko sends them to Beidou, whose ship is the Alcor.

Beidou holds the Crux Clash, a tournament for fighters without Visions, and Kazuha, a temporary crew member, supplies the prize: a Masterless Vision. If the Traveler wins, they can choose that or passage to Inazuma. When Fei the Flyer, a Treasure Hoarder, steals the Vision and is caught, he is disqualified and the Traveler is crowned champion.

Kazuha explains why the Vision matters: when the Raiden Shogun enacted the Vision Hunt Decree, a friend of his challenged her and died in the duel, and Kazuha took the friend's Vision and fled. He hopes someone can reawaken it. He warns the Traveler that Inazuma is dangerous and tells them the Alcor will be notified when it is ready, while he travels across Liyue.

Midsummer island adventure: During the limited-time event Midsummer Island Adventure, Klee receives a letter from a "Dodo-King" who threatens to take Dodoco from her. The Traveler, Paimon, Jean and Barbara go with her, carried by Dvalin at Venti's summons, and Kaeya, Diluc, Albedo and Razor follow separately.

According to the archipelago's history, the islands were formerly called the Haar Islands and were made when Barbatos reshaped Mondstadt. In the story it is revealed that Alice, Klee's mother, arranged the trip so her daughter could have a memorable summer. The event needed Adventure Rank 21 and the Archon Quest Song of the Dragon and Freedom.

Characters and content: Kaedehara Kazuha ("Scarlet Leaves Pursue Wild Waves") is a 5-star Anemo sword user. Banners were Sparkling Steps (Klee) in phase 1 and Leaves in the Wind (Kazuha, from 2021-06-29) in phase 2. New weapons were Freedom-Sworn, Mitternachts Waltz and Dodoco Tales.

Maguu Kenki was added as a monster. Other events were Never-Ending Battle, Kaboomball Kombat, Legend of the Vagabond Sword and Echoing Tales. The wiki also lists limited-time World Quests such as They Who Hear the Sea and Who Wields the Wild Wind?.

New outfits were Sea Breeze Dandelion for Jean and Summertime Sparkle for Barbara. The Spiral Abyss had new Lunar Phases themed on Swirl: Whirlpool Moon, Breezecall Moon and Brumous Moon.

How {{char}} behaves: Island events are canon but not universally known. Mention the Golden Apple Archipelago only for characters who were there, and use limited-time details with that caveat. Kazuha's backstory is learned in this version and should not be told by characters who have not heard it.

78.content: Version 1.6 (2021-06-09) introduced Kaedehara Kazuha, the Golden Apple Archipelago limited-time area and the Chapter II Prologue, Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves.

79.content:
Version 2.0: The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia (also: Version 2.0, Update 2.0, Patch 2.0): Version 2.0, "The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia", was released on 2021-07-21. It opened Inazuma, the Electro nation of the Raiden Shogun, and began Archon Quest Chapter II. It added Kamisato Ayaka, Yoimiya, Sayu and the Electro Traveler.

New areas: Narukami Island, Kannazuka and Yashiori Island. The Chapter II prologue came earlier in 1.6, so 2.0 delivered Act I, "The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia", and Act II, "Stillness, the Sublimation of Shadow".

The patch also launched Inazuma reputation, Thunder Sakura Boughs, Thunder Barriers, Balethunder and the Epitomized Path weapon-banner system. These are game features, not in-world facts.

Contents: Characters: Kamisato Ayaka (5-star Cryo sword), Yoimiya (5-star Pyro bow), Sayu (4-star Anemo claymore). Weapons: Thundering Pulse and Mistsplitter Reforged, plus forgeable Hamayumi, Amenoma Kageuchi, Kitain Cross Spear, Katsuragikiri Nagamasa and Hakushin Ring.

Banners: "The Heron's Court" (Ayaka) in phase 1; "Tapestry of Golden Flames" (Yoimiya and Sayu) from 2021-08-10. Artifact sets: Emblem of Severed Fate and Shimenawa's Reminiscence. Story quests: Grus Nivis Chapter Act I (Ayaka) and Carassius Auratus Chapter Act I (Yoimiya), both required for Act II.

Events were Thunder Sojourn, Lost Riches, Theater Mechanicus: Stage of Wonders, Phantom Flow and Ley Line Overflow, all limited-time. New foes included Kairagi, Nobushi, Mirror Maidens, the Pyro Hypostasis, Ruin Sentinels and Electro Samachurls.

Story: Act I: the Traveler reaches Ritou under the Sakoku Decree. Thoma helps them past the port, then reveals he serves the Kamisato Clan; Kamisato Ayaka quietly opposes the Vision Hunt Decree. Act II: Thoma is taken as the hundredth Vision Hunt victim, the Raiden Shogun declares the Traveler "an exception" and the "enemy of eternity", and the Traveler joins the Watatsumi Army's resistance.

Ayaka sends the Traveler to three people who lost their Visions, and then to free the craftsman Masakatsu with Yoimiya's help; Kujou Sara catches them but lets them go. After Thoma's rescue, the Traveler fights Sara in a ceremonial contest of honour, and Sangonomiya Kokomi arrives with mercenaries, among them Beidou and Kaedehara Kazuha, so Sara retreats.

The Shogun's reasons, the Fatui's role and the Plane of Euthymia are not revealed until Act III (2.1). Do not give characters Act III knowledge in a 2.0-period scene.

Placement: Follows 1.6 and precedes 2.1. The Sakoku Decree ended in the 2.5 story quest "Transient Dreams", and the Vision Hunt Decree ended after Act III in 2.1.

80.comment: Version 2.0: The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia: Version 2.0 Archon Quest Chapter II
80.content:
Act I, "The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia" (Adventure Rank 30), starts at Ritou, where foreign merchants of the International Trade Association, led by Kurisu, are squeezed by the Kanjou Commission, which demanded Crystal Marrow as tax. Thoma, backed by a Yashiro Commission card, forces the officers off. Commissioner Hiiragi Shinsuke stalls the Traveler's travel permit, and his daughter Hiiragi Chisato helps in secret; she says an arrogant-sounding woman, identified on the wiki as Signora, had arrived and conspired with her father.

Ayaka, speaking from behind a screen, sends the Traveler to three Vision-bearers: Tejima at Konda Village, the samurai Kurosawa Kyounosuke in Inazuma City, and the swordmaster Domon, whose case shows that losing a Vision can bring buried regrets back, not a demon. Yae Miko notes the Traveler with interest. In Act II the Traveler is a wanted criminal and Thoma retreats to Komore Teahouse, safe within Yashiro Commission territory.

Act II needs the Story Quests "The Whispers of the Crane and the White Rabbit" and "Dreamlike Timelessness", and is the shortest Archon Quest act (two quests). The Chapter II prologue "Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves" is a 1.6 quest.

81.comment: Version 2.0: The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia: Version 2.0 New Characters
81.content: Version 2.0 introduced Kamisato Ayaka, Yoimiya and Sayu as playable characters, and let the Traveler use Electro. In the story Ayaka is the Kamisato Clan's eldest daughter, the Shirasagi Himegimi, and Yoimiya is the Naganohara fireworks maker who, in Act I, helps a Vision-bearer hand over a fake Vision to the confiscating samurai. Thoma appears here as a Ritou contact but was not playable until 2.2; Sayu's story role comes in Act III (2.1). Banners were limited-time and have been rerun.

82.comment: Version 2.1: Floating World Under the Moonlight
82.content:
Version 2.1: Floating World Under the Moonlight (also: Version 2.1, Update 2.1, Patch 2.1, Floating World Under the Moonlight): Version 2.1, "Floating World Under the Moonlight", was released on 2021-09-01. It added Watatsumi Island and Seirai Island, the Archon Quest Chapter II Act III "Omnipresence Over Mortals", and the Raiden Shogun, Sangonomiya Kokomi and Kujou Sara. Aloy was PlayStation-only.

Act III ends the Shogun confrontation begun in 2.0: the Traveler exposes the Fatui's hand in the Vision Hunt war, duels Signora, and defeats the Raiden Shogun in the Plane of Euthymia, after which Ei agrees to abolish the Vision Hunt Decree.

The patch also added fishing, the Phase Gate and the Thunder Manifestation boss. Hyakunin Ikki and Moonlight Merriment events were limited-time.

Contents: Characters: Raiden Shogun (5-star Electro polearm), Sangonomiya Kokomi (5-star Hydro catalyst), Kujou Sara (4-star Electro bow), Aloy (5-star Cryo bow, PlayStation only). Weapons: Engulfing Lightning, Everlasting Moonglow, Luxurious Sea-Lord, "The Catch", Predator (PlayStation).

Banners: "Reign of Serenity" (Raiden Shogun and Kujou Sara) in phase 1 and "Drifting Luminescence" (Kokomi) from 2021-09-21. Bosses: La Signora (weekly, at Tenshukaku), the Hydro Hypostasis and the Thunder Manifestation. Story Quests: Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter Act I "Reflections of Mortality" (Raiden Shogun) and Dracaena Somnolenta Chapter Act I (Kokomi). The Seirai Stormchasers world quest series covers Seirai Island.

Limited events: Moonlight Merriment, Passage of Clouds and Stars, Hyakunin Ikki, Lunar Realm and Spectral Secrets.

Story: After Kokomi names the Traveler captain of a Resistance unit, the Fatui turn out to be the Resistance's mysterious sponsor and are supplying Delusions, which drain the user's life. The Traveler duels Signora before the Shogun, the Shogun kills her, and Kaedehara Kazuha helps block the Shogun's strike. In the Plane of Euthymia, Yae Miko persuades Ei to abolish the Vision Hunt Decree.

Teppei, a Resistance soldier, uses a Delusion and dies prematurely aged. Chapter II also shows Kujou Takayuki, head of the Kujou Clan, selling out the Shogunate to the Fatui. Yae Miko saved the Traveler from the Balladeer by giving him Ei's Electro Gnosis.

Ei's reasons for eternity are the deaths of companions and her sister Makoto, and watching Khaenri'ah's destruction by the Heavenly Principles. Miko also tells the Traveler that knowledge is managed as a resource in Sumeru, and suggests the Traveler lacks a Vision because they have not yet found an ambition strong enough.

Placement: Follows 2.0 and precedes 2.2. The Interlude Chapter Act I is 2.4. Sakoku ended in 2.5; the Archon Quest continues in Chapter II Act IV (2.6), then Sumeru in 3.0.

83.comment: Version 2.1: Floating World Under the Moonlight: Version 2.1 Archon Quest Chapter II Act III
83.content:
Act III has nine quests. Kokomi makes the Traveler captain of "Swordfish II". An anonymous sponsor has been supplying the Resistance, and the Traveler recognises one of its weapons as a Delusion. Teppei dies from using it. The Traveler dismantles the factory, where a Fatui mole named Nathan is revealed and where the Balladeer appears. Yae Miko rescues the Traveler and takes them to the Grand Narukami Shrine. She explains that the Shogun on the throne is a puppet, while Ei dwells in the Plane of Euthymia.

Miko trains the Traveler for the confrontation. To split the Tenryou Commission, the Traveler, with Yoimiya as a distraction and the Shuumatsuban ninja Sayu infiltrating, obtains Takayuki's falsified reports and correspondence with the Fatui. Kujou Sara reads them, confronts her adoptive father, and then races to Tenshukaku, where she is beaten by Signora. The Traveler duels Signora in the Shogun's presence, wins, and Signora is executed by the Shogun's Musou no Hitotachi. Kazuha resonates with his late friend's Masterless Vision to parry the Shogun's strike.

In the Plane, Ei confesses she had known about the Fatui. Miko enters the Plane through the omamori she gave the Traveler, and the light of the confiscated Visions outside brightens it. Ei concedes and promises to abolish the decree but says she needs time to reconsider how to rule. Miko discloses the Electro Gnosis trade, confirms the Balladeer was Ei's prototype puppet turned Sixth Harbinger (her claim), and speaks of Sumeru.

84.comment: Version 2.1: Floating World Under the Moonlight: Version 2.1 New Characters
84.content: Version 2.1 introduced the Raiden Shogun, Sangonomiya Kokomi and Kujou Sara, with Aloy as a PlayStation-only reward delivered by mail to Adventure Rank 20+ players. Kokomi is the Resistance's commander and Sara the Shogun's Army general; the Raiden Shogun is the Electro Archon. Banners were limited-time and have been rerun.

85.comment: Version 2.1: Floating World Under the Moonlight: Version 2.1 Watatsumi and Seirai Islands
85.content: Watatsumi Island is the Sangonomiya Clan's island at the far end of Inazuma from Narukami Island. It has dense, differently coloured foliage and a long-standing poor relationship with the Shogun's government. The Watatsumi Army rose against the Vision Hunt Decree. In Act III, the Tatarigami phenomenon, tied to the death of the god Orobashi in the Archon War, is mentioned near Fort Mumei. Seirai Island is a storm-ravaged island with Balethunder; in the Seirai Stormchasers series the Traveler seals four Warding Stones, meets the talking cat Neko at Asase Shrine, defeats a Thunder Manifestation, and finds a Peculiar Pinion.

86.content:
Version 2.2: Into the Perilous Labyrinth of Fog (also: Version 2.2, Update 2.2, Patch 2.2, Into the Perilous Labyrinth of Fog): Version 2.2, "Into the Perilous Labyrinth of Fog", was released on 2021-10-13. It added fog-bound Tsurumi Island, the playable Thoma, and Aloy for all platforms. It had no Archon Quest.

Tsurumi Island's story is told by the "Through the Mists" world quest series, which follows on from the Seirai Stormchasers of 2.1. It tells how a child's ceremony for the Thunderbird Kanna Kapatcir ended in a curse.

The patch also added the Silken Courtyard realm layout, rifthound enemies and Sacred Sakura's Favor level 40.

Contents: Characters: Thoma (4-star Pyro polearm); Aloy (5-star Cryo bow), previously PlayStation-only, now for all platforms. Weapons: Polar Star (5-star bow), Wavebreaker's Fin, Akuoumaru, Mouun's Moon.

Banners: "Farewell of Snezhnaya" (Tartaglia) in phase 1; "Moment of Bloom" (Hu Tao and Thoma) from 2021-11-02. Hangout events Series III: Sayu Act I "Yoohoo Art: Seichou no Jutsu" and Thoma Act I "A Housekeeper's Daily Chores". New enemies: Rockfond and Thundercraven Rifthounds and their whelps.

Events were Labyrinth Warriors, Shadow of the Ancients, Tuned to the World's Sounds, Dreams of Bloom and a Ley Line Overflow, all limited-time. Other world quests were The Saga of Mr. Forgetful and Clean House.

Story: No Archon Quest. The Traveler helps the novelist Sumida by going to Tsurumi Island, where the locals repeat a ceremony and the Maushiro keeps vanishing. The truth is that the child Ruu offered himself to the Thunderbird, who cursed the island to relive it. The Traveler lifts the curse by letting Ruu sing for her once more.

Kama's boat reaches the fog-bound island. The Peculiar Pinion found in Seirai (2.1) shows memories of the Thunderbird. Ruu offered himself because the island's situation was worsening. The Raiden Shogun had killed the Thunderbird, so the Traveler and Paimon say she has moved to Seirai Island, and the Pinion carries Ruu there to sing. With the loop over, Ruu will pass on.

Tsurumi Island also has a three-day cycle that changes enemy and chest spawns. This is a gameplay feature on the wiki, separate from the story.

Placement: Follows 2.1 and precedes 2.3. The Hu Tao banner also features Thoma. The quest series states that Kapatcir was killed by the Raiden Shogun.

87.comment: Version 2.2: Into the Perilous Labyrinth of Fog: Version 2.2 Tsurumi Island
87.content:
Tsurumi Island is a fog-shrouded island in Inazuma that once held two ancient civilisations: an underground Pre-Thunderbird one and the Thunderbird civilisation that worshipped Kanna Kapatcir. Its modern inhabitants are hilichurls, rifthounds and automatons. The fog is lifted by the quest series "Through the Mists". Its legend: a child, Ruu, offered himself to the Thunderbird, and she cursed the island to relive that ceremony until she heard his song again.

The series' parts: "A Particularly Particular Author", "Octave of the Maushiro", "The Sea of Fog and the Rite of the Trees", and "The Sun-Wheel and Mt. Kanna". Kama's ancestors came from Tsurumi, and Kama tells Ruu they lived happily elsewhere and only regretted not returning for him.

88.comment: Version 2.2: Into the Perilous Labyrinth of Fog: Version 2.2 New Characters
88.content: Version 2.2 made Thoma playable, a Kamisato Clan attendant already seen in 2.0 and 2.1, and extended Aloy to all platforms, delivered by mail at Adventure Rank 20 or above. The Hu Tao banner ran beside Thoma's. Banners were limited-time and have been rerun.

89.content:
Version 2.3: Shadows Amidst Snowstorms (also: Version 2.3, Shadows Amidst Snowstorms (version), 2.3 update): Version 2.3, Shadows Amidst Snowstorms, was released on 2021-11-24. It brought two new characters, Arataki Itto and Gorou. It had no Archon Quest and no new region.

Its flagship event, also called Shadows Amidst Snowstorms, was set on Dragonspine. The official blurb is mock-mysterious and ends by saying it has "absolutely nothing to do" with Itto, leader of the Arataki Gang.

The event was a limited-time flagship event, and it gave away a 4-star sword, Cinnabar Spindle, as its reward.

Because the version has no Archon Quest, it does not move the main story; its events are canon but limited.

Characters: Arataki Itto ("Hanamizaka Heroics", 5-star Geo claymore) and Gorou ("Canine Warrior", 4-star Geo bow) were released with the Oni's Royale banner in phase 2, starting 2021-12-14. Phase 1 reran Secretum Secretorum (Albedo) and Born of Ocean Swell (Eula).

New equipment: Redhorn Stonethresher (5-star claymore), Cinnabar Spindle (4-star sword) and the artifact sets Husk of Opulent Dreams and Ocean-Hued Clam.

Story quests and hangouts: Itto's Taurus Iracundus Chapter Act I, Rise Up, Golden Soul; Gorou's Hangout Event Act I, The Canine General's Special Operations; and Beidou's Hangout Event Act I, When the Crux Shines Bright. The Golden Wolflord was added as a monster, with a new gadget, Omni-Ubiquity Net, and a new domain, Slumbering Court.

Shadows amidst snowstorms: This flagship event ran from 2021-11-25 to 2021-12-13 on Dragonspine, and the event shop stayed open until 2021-12-20. Its three acts were The Snowy Past, The Shadows Deepen and A Secret Born From Ashes, unlocked on 2021-11-25, 2021-12-01 and 2021-12-04. It required Adventure Rank 20, For a Tomorrow Without Tears, Albedo's Princeps Cretaceus Chapter Act I and Joel's Lost in the Snow.

Gameplay was built around three modes: Born of the Snow, in which players build puffy snowmen at the camp; Dragonspine Special Training; and Rise of the Fell Flower. Snowman parts were the event's cosmetic reward, and they could be taken into the Serenitea Pot afterwards.

Other content: Other events were Bantan Sango Case Files: The Warrior Dog, Misty Dungeon: Realm of Light, Energy Amplifier Fruition and a Marvelous Merchandise rerun. World Quests included Omni-Ubiquity Net and Snowy Silhouette: Hope and Reunion. Companion furnishings were added for Paimon, Itto and Gorou.

The Spiral Abyss floor 11 Ley Line Disorder was changed to increase Geo DMG and Physical DMG for all party members. These are gameplay notes, not lore.

How {{char}} behaves: Dragonspine winter events are canon but limited-time, so only characters who joined in should refer to them. Itto and Gorou are new faces in this version and should not be given Archon Quest knowledge they did not witness.

90.content: Version 2.3 (2021-11-24) added Arataki Itto and Gorou and the Dragonspine event Shadows Amidst Snowstorms. It had no Archon Quest and no new region.

91.content:
Version 2.4: Fleeting Colors in Flight (also: Version 2.4, Update 2.4, Patch 2.4): Version 2.4, "Fleeting Colors in Flight", was released on 2022-01-05. It opened Enkanomiya beneath Watatsumi Island, began the Interlude Chapter with Act I "The Crane Returns on the Wind", and added Shenhe and Yun Jin.

The Interlude Act I is set in Liyue, where Ningguang rebuilds the Jade Chamber and the Traveler meets Shenhe, a human raised by the adeptus Cloud Retainer. Enkanomiya, a hidden underground realm of Inazuma's Watatsumi people, is opened by world quests.

The patch is mostly a Liyue-and-Inazuma release: Zhongli, Ganyu and Xiao had banners again, and six existing characters received new outfits.

Contents: Characters: Shenhe (5-star Cryo polearm) and Yun Jin (4-star Geo polearm). Weapon: Calamity Queller (5-star polearm). New area: Enkanomiya.

Banners: "The Transcendent One Returns" (Shenhe and Yun Jin) and "Invitation to Mundane Life" (Xiao and Yun Jin) in phase 1; "Gentry of Hermitage" (Zhongli) and "Adrift in the Harbor" (Ganyu) from 2022-01-25. Hangout events Series V: Ningguang Act I "The Jade Chamber's Returning Guest" and Yun Jin Act I "A Song That Knows Grace". Enemies: Abyss Lector: Fathomless Flames, Specters, Bathysmal Vishaps, Coral Defenders.

Events were Fleeting Colors in Flight, Prosperous Partnerships, May Fortune Find You, Flowing Lights and Colors, A Study in Potions, Eight Locales Over Mountains and Seas and Windtrace, all limited-time. Outfits: Ningguang, Keqing, Amber, Jean, Mona and Rosaria. The Sacred Sakura's Favor level cap rose to 50.

Story: Ningguang announces a contest: the first three people to bring Sunset Vermillionite, Wonder Cores and Adepti Sigils get an honest answer to any question. The Traveler teams up with Shenhe and Yun Jin, wins, and the Jade Chamber ascends. Beisht, Osial's wife, attacks, and Ningguang's defences, the Millelith and Beidou's fleet drive it off with Shenhe's help.

Cloud Retainer reveals Shenhe is human, not an adeptus, and says the adepti sense a coming calamity and would take control of Liyue if Ningguang cannot handle it. Yun Jin's opera "The Divine Damsel of Devastation" turns out to be based on Shenhe's own life. At the banquet, Yun Jin performs it on the Jade Chamber.

Ningguang cannot find a lead on the Traveler's sibling, so she answers Paimon's question instead. Shenhe asks how to fit in in Liyue Harbor, and Ningguang suggests building a sense of belonging.

Placement: Follows 2.3 and precedes 2.5. The Interlude Chapter continues with Act II, "Perilous Trail", in 2.7.

key: The Crane Returns on the Wind
92.comment: Version 2.4: Fleeting Colors in Flight: Version 2.4 Interlude Chapter Act I
92.content:
The Crane Returns on the Wind has four quests: "Jade Chamber Rising", "Seagaze Sunset", "Bygones Times Like Dust Passing" and "Where the Heart Finds Rest". Shenhe, new to the city, is almost cheated by two brokers, then eats herbs like Qingxin and Violetgrass at Bubu Pharmacy. The Traveler secures Sunset Vermillionite from Sea Gazer's abode (guided by Xingqiu and the Feiyun Commerce Guild), Starsplinter Iron and Subrosium for the Wonder Cores, and Shenhe crafts the sigils.

Beidou introduces Yun Jin, whose opera is to be staged on the Jade Chamber. Mingjun, a villager, is surprised that the rumoured Shenhe is alive. The Traveler reads Yun Jin's father's diary and realises the opera's heroine is Shenhe, who says she prefers the opera's version of herself. After Beisht's defeat, Zhu Tao, drunk, bothers the group and is rebuked by Shenhe.

93.comment: Version 2.4: Fleeting Colors in Flight: Version 2.4 Enkanomiya
93.content:
Enkanomiya is a subterranean realm under Watatsumi Island, entered by a deep pool east of Sangonomiya Shrine. Its entrance needs the Key of the Moon-Bathed Deep, made from pearls in five shrines, plus unlocking requirements (Adventure Rank 30, "Ritou Escape Plan" and "The Still Water's Flow"). A light mechanism, the Dainichi Mikoshi, switches the realm between Whitenight and Evernight. Wiki lore says it was once called Byakuyakoku; the god Orobashi saved its people by leading them up to the surface. The Watatsumi people descend from them.

The realm's quests mention the Abyss Order seeking the book "Before Sun and Moon" for a figure called Enjou. The Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri uses a branch from Enkanomiya, and after the Three Realms Gateway Offering (a limited-time event in 2.5) Kokomi looks for another approach.

94.comment: Version 2.4: Fleeting Colors in Flight: Version 2.4 New Characters
94.content: Version 2.4 introduced Shenhe, a human disciple of Cloud Retainer, and Yun Jin, a Liyue opera director. Banners were limited-time and have been rerun.

95.content:
Version 2.5: When the Sakura Bloom (also: Version 2.5, Update 2.5, Patch 2.5, When the Sakura Bloom): Version 2.5, "When the Sakura Bloom", was released on 2022-02-16. It added Yae Miko, Kagura's Verity and two Inazuma Story Quests. It had no new region or Archon Quest.

"Transient Dreams" resolves Ei's reconsideration of eternity and ends with the abolition of the Sakoku Decree. "The Great Narukami Offering" is Yae Miko's first Story Quest and involves a rumoured wish-granting book.

The patch also introduced the Magatsu Mitake Narukami no Mikoto weekly boss and the Trounce Domain "End of the Oneiric Euthymia", where the Shogun puppet can be fought again.

Contents: Character: Yae Miko (5-star Electro catalyst). Weapons: Kagura's Verity (5-star catalyst) and Oathsworn Eye (4-star catalyst). Banner: "Everbloom Violet" (Yae Miko) in phase 1.

Phase 2 reran "Reign of Serenity" (Raiden Shogun) and "Drifting Luminescence" (Sangonomiya Kokomi) from 2022-03-08. New enemies: Shadowy Husks (Standard Bearer, Line Breaker, Defender). A new Coral Butterfly was added.

Events: Three Realms Gateway Offering, Divine Ingenuity, Of Drink A-Dreaming, Hyakunin Ikki (from 2022-03-18) and Overflowing Mastery (from 2022-03-21), all limited-time.

Story: Rifthounds attack the Sacred Sakura, and Ei appears to help the Traveler defend it. The Sacred Sakura's roots manifest memories of the Khaenri'ah cataclysm 500 years ago, when monsters also struck Inazuma and Kitsune Saiguu died leading its defence. Ei duels her Shogun puppet inside Makoto's consciousness, wins, and then offers it a role as her kagemusha. She abolishes the Sakoku Decree.

Makoto's fragment, kept in the sword Musou Isshin, apologises to Ei for suddenly handing her the rulership and for not persuading her gently, and gives her a seed that grows into the Sacred Sakura. Before the duel, Ei had sent the Traveler to tell Yae Miko to govern Inazuma in her stead.

Gameplay note: after the quest, the "A Nation Closed by Thunder" climate ends and travellers can leave Inazuma by sea freely. In "The Great Narukami Offering", Miko recognises the wish-granting book's summoning spirit as her friend Urakusai, who meant no harm and wanted youkai to leave life without regrets; a Hyakkiyakou is held in farewell.

Placement: Follows 2.4 and precedes 2.6. Both Story Quests require Adventure Rank 40 and Chapter II Act III; Transient Dreams also requires Reflections of Mortality, and Miko's quest requires Transient Dreams. Yae Miko appears later as a guest star in 7.1's Imaginarium Theater.

96.comment: Version 2.5: When the Sakura Bloom: Version 2.5 Transient Dreams
96.content:
Transient Dreams is the second act of the Raiden Shogun's Story Quest, the Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter. Its quests are "Cleansing Light", "Farewell to the Past" and "Radiant Sakura". Ei joins the Traveler in tracking rifthounds around the Sacred Sakura and Araumi, meets echoes of the 500-year-old cataclysm, and shares that Makoto went to Khaenri'ah without telling her and died; she then decided to pursue eternity.

Ei describes the Sacred Sakura as a tree that purifies the ley lines, whose roots can evoke memories. Furuyama's tea set, Kitamura, Fujiki and Fukami all appear as echoes. She is taken to a cave beneath the Grand Narukami Shrine for her duel. The Shogun puppet thinks she has fallen to erosion; the Traveler returns later and the duel ends. Afterwards Ei looks at Inazuma's current state and abolishes the Sakoku Decree.

97.comment: Version 2.5: When the Sakura Bloom: Version 2.5 Yae Miko and The Great Narukami Offering
97.content: Version 2.5 introduced Yae Miko, the Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine, who also runs Yae Publishing House. Her Story Quest "The Great Narukami Offering" has four quests: "Mysterious Urban Legend", "Friendship in Writing", "A Centuries-Long Dream" and "Banquet of Parting". A book on summoning spirits causes odd behaviour; the Traveler and Miko write a rival novel, trace the author, and learn that the spirit, Urakusai, meant no harm. The banner was limited-time and has been rerun.

key: Version 2.6: Zephyr of the Violet Garden
98.comment: Version 2.6: Zephyr of the Violet Garden
98.content:
Version 2.6: Zephyr of the Violet Garden (also: Version 2.6, Zephyr of the Violet Garden, Genshin Impact 2.6): Version 2.6, "Zephyr of the Violet Garden", was released on 2022-03-30. Its headline content was the playable Inazuman Kamisato Ayato, The Chasm as a Liyue subregion, and Archon Quest Chapter II Act IV, "Requiem of the Echoing Depths", set in the Chasm's depths.

The Archon Quest sends the Traveler and Dainsleif into the underground mines, where the Abyss Order is at work in an inverted city and the Black Serpent Knights still guard the people of Khaenri'ah.

Contents: New character: Kamisato Ayato ("Pillar of Fortitude", 5-star Hydro Sword). New weapon: Haran Geppaku Futsu (5-star Sword). New artifact sets: Vermillion Hereafter and Echoes of an Offering. New subregion: The Chasm, with a new domain, The Lost Valley. Event wishes: Azure Excursion (Ayato) and Ballad in Goblets (Venti) in phase 1, The Heron's Court (Kamisato Ayaka) in phases 2 and 3.

New enemies: Ruin Serpent, Black Serpent Knight: Windcutter and Floating Hydro Fungus; new wildlife included the Bluethunder Weasel and Lucklight Fly. The Lumenstone Adjuvant gadget and the Starshroom item were added, and Radiant Spincrystals appeared in Mondstadt, Liyue and Inazuma. World Quest series included The Chasm Delvers and Valor's Afterglow.

Events were Hues of the Violet Garden and Outside the Canvas, Inside the Lens (phase 1), Vibro-Crystal Research, Ley Line Overflow and Marvelous Merchandise (phase 2), and Spices From the West and Overflowing Mastery (phase 3). Other changes included Tutorials improvements, alternate-outfit voice lines for Jean, Amber, Rosaria and Mona, and a separate "Chasmlighter" achievement category for exploring the Chasm.

Story: Archon Quest Chapter II Act IV, "Requiem of the Echoing Depths", has the Traveler and Paimon take a miner's request about odd hilichurl activity in the Chasm. Underground they find an Inverted City and meet Dainsleif, who explains that "Twilight Sword" was his title as captain of Khaenri'ah's Royal Guard five hundred years earlier. Hilichurls gather in the area to live out their last days, and the place seems to ease the Khaenri'ahn curse.

Black Serpent Knights, once Dainsleif's subordinates and now mindless from the curse, guard those hilichurls. One knight, whom Dainsleif believes to be Halfdan, restrains the others and leads the party to a hilichurl camp. There the Traveler sees a vision, through an Inteyvat flower, of their sibling and an Abyss Herald planning to amplify a water pool's properties to lift the curse from the gathered hilichurls. Dainsleif judges this futile and harmful, and the Traveler chooses to help him stop it.

An Abyss Lector triggers an amplification device that causes agony to those afflicted by the curse. Halfdan sacrifices himself to halt it long enough for the Traveler to defeat the Lector and destroy the mechanism. His soul briefly speaks with Dainsleif before departing. Dainsleif then leaves to recover and to look into the Abyss Order's Loom of Fate project. The Story Quest Cypressus Custos Chapter Act I, "The Firmiana Leaf Falls", was also added in this version.

Placement: Follows 2.5 and precedes 2.7. The Chasm's story continues in the 2.7 Interlude Chapter Act II, "Perilous Trail".

99.comment: Version 2.6: Zephyr of the Violet Garden: Requiem of the Echoing Depths
99.content: Archon Quest Chapter II Act IV, released in 2.6. The Traveler and Dainsleif investigate the Chasm's Inverted City. Black Serpent Knights guard dying hilichurls; Halfdan sacrifices himself to stop an Abyss Order amplification device.

100.comment: Version 2.6: Zephyr of the Violet Garden: Version 2.6 Zephyr of the Violet Garden
100.content: Version 2.6 (2022-03-30): Kamisato Ayato, The Chasm as a subregion, and Archon Quest Chapter II Act IV.

key: Version 2.7: Hidden Dreams in the Depths
101.comment: Version 2.7: Hidden Dreams in the Depths
101.content:
Version 2.7: Hidden Dreams in the Depths (also: Version 2.7, Hidden Dreams in the Depths, Genshin Impact 2.7): Version 2.7, "Hidden Dreams in the Depths", was released on 2022-05-31. It added the playable Yelan (5-star Hydro Bow) and Kuki Shinobu (4-star Electro Sword) and Archon Quest Interlude Chapter Act II, "Perilous Trail", in which a party is trapped in the depths of The Chasm. It opened no new region.

Yelan's Story Quest (Umbrabilis Orchis Chapter Act I, "Calculated Gambit") and a Kuki Shinobu Hangout Event also released with the version.

Contents: New characters: Yelan ("Valley Orchid", 5-star Hydro Bow) and Kuki Shinobu ("Mender of Tribulations", 4-star Electro Sword). New weapons: Aqua Simulacra (5-star Bow) and Fading Twilight (4-star Bow). Event wishes: Discerner of Enigmas (Yelan) and a rerun of Invitation to Mundane Life (Xiao) in phase 1; Oni's Royale (Arataki Itto and Kuki Shinobu) in phase 2.

Quests: Interlude Chapter Act II "Perilous Trail"; Yelan's Story Quest "Calculated Gambit"; Kuki Shinobu's Hangout Event Act I "The Gang's Daily Deeds"; World Quests "On the Stage, Behind the Stage", "The Tales Behind the Fan" and "Garcia's Paean". New recipes were Dew-Dipped Shrimp and Omurice Waltz.

Events: Perilous Trail (event), A Muddy Bizarre Adventure, The Almighty Arataki Great and Glorious Drumalong Festival and Core of the Apparatus. Other additions were character level-up guides with talent and artifact main-attribute recommendations, and the Floral Zither gadget becoming purchasable from Granny Shan in Liyue Harbor.

Story: In "Perilous Trail" (Interlude Chapter Act II), the Traveler and Paimon return to the Chasm after earlier events there and meet Yanfei, Arataki Itto, Kuki Shinobu and Yelan. A crack in the ground drops the group into The Chasm's Bed, where they enter a strange domain that turns out to prey on the fears and weaknesses of whoever enters. Xiao appears, saying he is looking for someone.

Xiao explains that he seeks his missing brother-in-arms Bosacius, and the domain proves to be a chaotic, illusion-filled space. The party works through it using Yanfei's theory that its own rules can be turned against it, and finds a Fantastic Compass that helps them get back to the surface. In "Calculated Gambit", Yelan is helping Uncle Tian, the Tianshu of the Liyue Qixing, assess three candidates for his successor.

Placement: Follows 2.6 and precedes 2.8. "Perilous Trail" requires earlier quests including the Interlude Chapter's first act, and leads into the Interlude Chapter's next act, "Inversion of Genesis".

102.comment: Version 2.7: Hidden Dreams in the Depths: Perilous Trail
102.content: Interlude Chapter Act II, released in 2.7 (the similarly named event is separate). The Traveler, Yanfei, Yelan, Arataki Itto and Kuki Shinobu are trapped in a chaotic domain beneath the Chasm and are joined by Xiao, who is searching for Bosacius.

103.comment: Version 2.7: Hidden Dreams in the Depths: Version 2.7 Hidden Dreams in the Depths
103.content: Version 2.7 (2022-05-31): Yelan and Kuki Shinobu, Interlude Chapter Act II "Perilous Trail", and no new region.

104.content:
Version 2.8: Summer Fantasia (also: Version 2.8, Summer Fantasia, 2.8 update): Version 2.8, Summer Fantasia, was released on 2022-07-13. It introduced Shikanoin Heizou and brought back the limited-time Golden Apple Archipelago for the summer event Summertime Odyssey. It had no Archon Quest and no new region.

Summertime Odyssey ran from 2022-07-15 until the end of the version and offered Fischl as its event reward. The official blurb mentions a cursed blade of unknown origin, an unsolved case and "familiar but not too familiar" islands at sea.

The archipelago returned with a different look from its first appearance in Version 1.6; the 2.8 map includes Minacious Isle.

New outfits were Ein Immernachtstraum for Fischl and Red Dead of Night for Diluc.

Characters and banners: Shikanoin Heizou ("Analytical Harmony") is a 4-star Anemo catalyst user. Phase 1 banners were Leaves in the Wind (Kaedehara Kazuha and Heizou) and Sparkling Steps (Klee and Heizou); phase 2, from 2022-08-02, was Tapestry of Golden Flames (Yoimiya).

New weapons were Kagotsurube Isshin (4-star sword) and two quest-exclusive 4-star swords, Prized Isshin Blade (Awakened) and Prized Isshin Blade (Shattered).

Story and hangout quests: Kazuha's Acer Palmatum Chapter Act I, A Strange and Friendless Road, and Heizou's Hangout Event Series VII Act I, Trap 'Em by Storm. New content also included the recipe The Only Truth and the namecard Shikanoin Heizou: Temari.

Summertime odyssey: The flagship event Summertime Odyssey required Adventure Rank 32, the Chapter II Prologue Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves, and Mona's Astrolabos Chapter Act I (or a Quick Start). It had two parts: Surfpiercer and a series of Phantom Realm challenges (Misty Hills, Foggy Vales; The Islands' Stirring Strings; Immernachtreich Keep; Temple of the Star Latitudes).

In the event, Fischl receives an important missive and sets out with everyone in town on another sojourn. Players collect Iridescent Flotsam to invite Fischl and to buy rewards.
